You are part of a data-center team responsible for server maintenance. Management wants a predictive-maintenance solution that uses monitoring data to identify possible server failures. The incident data has not yet been labeled. What should you do first?

options.text: Train a time-series model to predict the machines’ performance values. Configure an alert if a machine’s actual performance values significantly differ from the predicted performance values.
Develop a simple heuristic (e.g., based on z-score) to label the machines’ historical performance data. Use this heuristic to monitor server performance in real time.
Develop a simple heuristic (e.g., based on z-score) to label the machines’ historical performance data. Train a model to predict anomalies based on this labeled dataset.
Hire a team of qualified analysts to review and label the machines’ historical performance data. Train a model based on this manually labeled dataset.

questions.explanation:
Unlabeled monitoring data supports an unsupervised time-series anomaly-detection approach. A forecasting model establishes the expected performance pattern, and a significant difference between actual and predicted values indicates unusual behavior that may precede a server failure. Google Cloud documentation states that anomaly detection can use unsupervised machine learning when labeled data is unavailable.

**Learn more:** [Anomaly detection overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/anomaly-detection-overview) · [Timeseries Insights API concepts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/timeseries-insights/docs/concept)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team is experimenting with developing smaller, distilled LLMs for a particular domain. You have run batch inference on a dataset using several versions of your distilled LLMs and stored the batch-inference outputs in Cloud Storage. You need to build an evaluation workflow that integrates with your existing Vertex AI pipeline to evaluate the LLM versions’ performance while tracking artifacts. What should you do?

options.text: Develop a custom Python component that reads the batch inference outputs from Cloud Storage, calculates evaluation metrics, and writes the results to a BigQuery table.
Use a Dataflow component that processes the batch inference outputs from Cloud Storage, calculates evaluation metrics in a distributed manner, and writes the results to a BigQuery table.
Create a custom Vertex AI Pipelines component that reads the batch inference outputs from Cloud Storage, calculates evaluation metrics, and writes the results to a BigQuery table.
Use the Automatic side-by-side (AutoSxS) pipeline component that processes the batch inference outputs from Cloud Storage, aggregates evaluation metrics, and writes the results to a BigQuery table.

questions.explanation:
Automatic side-by-side (AutoSxS) is a managed pairwise model-evaluation pipeline that can evaluate pre-generated predictions stored as JSONL in Cloud Storage. It produces per-example judgments and aggregate win-rate metrics, exposes these as pipeline artifacts, and can write judgments to a BigQuery table.

**Learn more:** [Run AutoSxS pipeline to perform pairwise model-based evaluation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/side-by-side-eval?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team must build a model to predict whether images contain a driver's license, passport, or credit card. The data engineering team has already created the pipeline and generated a dataset consisting of 10,000 images with driver's licenses, 1,000 images with passports, and 1,000 images with credit cards. You now need to train a model using the following label map: [`˜drivers_license', `˜passport', `˜credit_card']. Which loss function should be used?

options.text: Categorical hinge
Binary cross-entropy
Categorical cross-entropy
Sparse categorical cross-entropy

questions.explanation:
Categorical cross-entropy trains a mutually exclusive multiclass classifier by comparing the predicted probability distribution over the three document classes with a one-hot target vector. TensorFlow documents categorical cross-entropy for one-hot true targets; sparse categorical cross-entropy is the alternative only when targets are represented as integer class IDs.

**Learn more:** [TensorFlow categorical cross-entropy](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/keras/losses/categorical_crossentropy) · [TensorFlow sparse categorical cross-entropy](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/keras/losses/SparseCategoricalCrossentropy)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a predictive-maintenance model to proactively identify component defects in bridges. You intend to use high-definition images of the bridges as inputs to the model. You must explain the model’s output to the relevant stakeholders so they can take suitable action. How should you build the model?

options.text: Use scikit-learn to build a tree-based model, and use SHAP values to explain the model output.
Use scikit-learn to build a tree-based model, and use partial dependence plots (PDP) to explain the model output.
Use TensorFlow to create a deep learning-based model, and use Integrated Gradients to explain the model output.
Use TensorFlow to create a deep learning-based model, and use the sampled Shapley method to explain the model output.

questions.explanation:
High-definition images are best handled by a deep learning model such as a TensorFlow neural network. Integrated Gradients explains predictions from differentiable models by assigning attribution scores to input features; for image classifiers, these features are pixels, so the attributions can show the image regions that drove a defect prediction. TensorFlow documents Integrated Gradients as applicable to differentiable models, including images, and demonstrates pixel-level feature importance for image classification.

**Learn more:** [Integrated gradients | TensorFlow Core](https://www.tensorflow.org/tutorials/interpretability/integrated_gradients) · [Use TensorFlow for explanations | Vertex AI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/explainable-ai/tensorflow)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an ML model to classify whether X-ray images show bone-fracture risk. You trained a ResNet architecture on Vertex AI with a TPU accelerator, but you are dissatisfied with its training time and memory consumption. You want to iterate on the training code quickly while making minimal code changes, and you also want to minimize the impact on model accuracy. What should you do?

options.text: Reduce the number of layers in the model architecture.
Reduce the global batch size from 1024 to 256.
Reduce the dimensions of the images used in the model.
Configure your model to use bfloat16 instead of float32.

questions.explanation:
On Cloud TPUs, bfloat16 has the same dynamic range as float32 while using half the memory. Explicitly using bfloat16 can reduce memory traffic and improve training performance, while TPU matrix multiplications use bfloat16 with float32 accumulation to preserve accuracy.

**Learn more:** [Improve your model's performance with bfloat16](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tpu/docs/bfloat16)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are an AI engineer at an apparel retail company. The sales team has identified seasonal sales patterns over the last 5–6 years. The team analyzes and visualizes weekly sales data that is stored in CSV files.  
  
You have been asked to estimate weekly sales for upcoming seasons to optimize inventory and personnel workloads. You want to use the most efficient approach. What should you do?

options.text: Upload the files into Cloud Storage. Use Python to preprocess and load the tabular data into BigQuery. Use time series forecasting models to predict weekly sales.

Upload the files into Cloud Storage. Use Python to preprocess and load the tabular data into BigQuery. Train a logistic regression model by using BigQuery ML to predict each product's weekly sales as one of three categories: high, medium, or low.

Load the files into BigQuery. Preprocess data by using BigQuery SQL. Connect BigQuery to Looker. Create a Looker dashboard that shows weekly sales trends in real time and can slice and dice the data based on relevant filters.

Create a custom conversational application using Vertex AI Agent Builder. Include code that enables file upload functionality, and upload the files. Use few-shot prompting and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to predict future sales trends by using the Gemini large language model (LLM).

questions.explanation:
Time-series forecasting is designed to predict future numeric values from historical observations and can model seasonal patterns in weekly sales data. BigQuery ML supports time-series forecasting with ARIMA_PLUS models, including forecasting future values from historical time-series columns.

**Learn more:** [Forecasting overview | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/forecasting-overview) · [The CREATE MODEL statement for ARIMA_PLUS models | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-create-time-series)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work on an operations team at an international company that manages a large fleet of on-premises servers in a few data centers worldwide. Your team gathers monitoring data from the servers, including CPU and memory consumption. When an incident happens on a server, your team is responsible for resolving it. Incident data has not yet been properly labeled.  
  
Your management team wants you to build a predictive-maintenance solution that uses monitoring data from the VMs to identify potential failures and alert the service desk team. What should you do first?

options.text: Train a time-series model to predict the machines’ performance values. Configure an alert if a machine’s actual performance values significantly differ from the predicted performance values.
Implement a simple heuristic (e.g., based on z-score) to label the machines’ historical performance data. Train a model to predict anomalies based on this labeled dataset.
Develop a simple heuristic (e.g., based on z-score) to label the machines’ historical performance data. Test this heuristic in a production environment.
Hire a team of qualified analysts to review and label the machines’ historical performance data. Train a model based on this manually labeled dataset.

questions.explanation:
When incident outcomes are not labeled, the initial detection approach should be a simple, explainable heuristic that can be evaluated against real operational outcomes. Running the heuristic in production establishes its alert quality and creates validated feedback for future training. Training a classifier on labels generated only by that same heuristic provides no independent ground truth and generally only automates the heuristic’s own errors. Google Cloud guidance distinguishes supervised predictive-maintenance approaches, which require labeled failure data, from anomaly-detection methods that can identify unusual behavior without labels.

**Learn more:** [A process for implementing industrial predictive maintenance: Part II](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/a-process-for-implementing-industrial-predictive-maintenance-part-ii) · [Supervised vs. unsupervised learning](https://cloud.google.com/discover/supervised-vs-unsupervised-learning)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have developed an application that uses a chain of multiple scikit-learn models to predict the optimal price for your company’s products. The workflow logic is shown below. Individual models are also used by members of your team in other solution workflows. You want to deploy this workflow while maintaining version control for every individual model and for the overall workflow. Your application must be able to scale down to zero. You want to minimize compute-resource usage and the manual effort needed to manage this solution. What should you do?  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783861283974-97x0h7gw.png)

options.text: Expose each individual model as an endpoint in Vertex AI Endpoints. Create a custom container endpoint to orchestrate the workflow.
Create a custom container endpoint for the workflow that loads each model’s individual files Track the versions of each individual model in BigQuery.
Expose each individual model as an endpoint in Vertex AI Endpoints. Use Cloud Run to orchestrate the workflow.
Load each model’s individual files into Cloud Run. Use Cloud Run to orchestrate the workflow. Track the versions of each individual model in BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
Vertex AI Endpoints allow the individual reusable models to be served independently, while Vertex AI Model Registry supports model-version management. Cloud Run is a fully managed orchestration service that automatically scales to zero when idle, minimizing idle compute use. Each Cloud Run deployment produces an immutable revision, providing version control for the orchestration workflow.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Run autoscaling](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-instance-autoscaling) · [Manage Cloud Run revisions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/managing/revisions)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a system-log anomaly-detection model for a cybersecurity organization. You built the model with TensorFlow and intend to use it for real-time prediction. You need to create a Dataflow pipeline that ingests data through Pub/Sub and writes results to BigQuery. You want to minimize serving latency as much as possible. What should you do?

options.text: Containerize the model prediction logic in Cloud Run, which is invoked by Dataflow.
Load the model directly into the Dataflow job as a dependency, and use it for prediction.
Deploy the model to a Vertex AI endpoint, and invoke this endpoint in the Dataflow job.
Deploy the model in a TFServing container on Google Kubernetes Engine, and invoke it in the Dataflow job.

questions.explanation:
Local TensorFlow inference on Dataflow workers eliminates the remote prediction-service call and its associated network and request overhead. Dataflow ML supports running TensorFlow models within the pipeline, and its local-inference features are optimized for worker memory management, throughput, and latency.

**Learn more:** [About Dataflow ML](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/machine-learning/ml-about) · [RunInference transform best practices](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/machine-learning/runinference-best-practices)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have deployed a conversational application that uses a large language model (LLM). The application has 1,000 users. You gather user feedback on the verbosity and accuracy of the model's responses. The feedback shows that responses are factually correct, but users prefer varying levels of verbosity based on the type of question.  
  
You want the model to produce responses that more consistently meet user expectations, using a scalable solution. What should you do?

options.text: Implement a keyword-based routing layer. If the user's input contains the words

Ask users to provide examples of responses with the appropriate verbosity as a list of question and answer pairs. Use this dataset to perform supervised fine tuning of the foundational model. Re-evaluate the verbosity of responses with the tuned model.

Ask users to indicate all scenarios where they expect concise responses versus verbose responses. Modify the application 's prompt to include these scenarios and their respective verbosity levels. Re-evaluate the verbosity of responses with updated prompts.
Experiment with other proprietary and open-source LLMs. Perform A/B testing by setting each model as your application's default model. Choose a model based on the results.

questions.explanation:
Supervised fine-tuning learns desired model behavior from labeled prompt-and-response examples. A dataset of user questions paired with responses at the appropriate verbosity can teach the model to produce consistent style and detail levels across the relevant question types at inference time. AWS documentation identifies supervised fine-tuning as appropriate for clear desired outputs and formatting or style consistency.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a rapidly expanding social media company. Your team develops TensorFlow recommender models in an on-premises CPU cluster. The data includes billions of historical user events and 100,000 categorical features. You observe that model-training time rises as the data grows. You plan to move the models to Google Cloud. You want the most scalable approach that also minimizes training time. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy the training jobs by using TPU VMs with TPUv3 Pod slices, and use the TPUEmbeading API
Deploy the training jobs in an autoscaling Google Kubernetes Engine cluster with CPUs
Deploy a matrix factorization model training job by using BigQuery ML
Deploy the training jobs by using Compute Engine instances with A100 GPUs, and use the tf.nn.embedding_lookup API

questions.explanation:
TPU Pod slices scale training across interconnected TPU chips, while the TPUEmbedding API is designed to train very large embedding tables on TPUs. This directly addresses the large categorical-feature and recommender workload, where distributed embedding lookups can otherwise become a training bottleneck.

**Learn more:** [About TPUs on Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/tpus/overview) · [tf.tpu.experimental.embedding.TPUEmbedding](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/tpu/experimental/embedding/TPUEmbedding)

options.text: Monitor the training/serving skew of feature values for requests sent to the endpoint.
Monitor the resource utilization of the endpoint, such as CPU and memory usage, to identify potential bottlenecks in performance.
Enable Vertex Explainable AI feature attribution to analyze model predictions and understand the impact of each feature on the model's predictions.
Monitor the latency of the endpoint to determine whether predictions are being served within the expected time frame.

questions.explanation:
A substantial decline in production AUC can result from training-serving skew: live input-feature distributions or feature processing differ from the training baseline. Monitoring the feature values in requests sent to the endpoint identifies such skew and helps isolate the features whose changed distributions may be degrading predictive performance. Resource utilization and latency concern serving capacity, while feature attribution explains individual outputs rather than detecting a shift between training and serving data.

**Learn more:** [Provide schemas to Vertex AI Model Monitoring](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/model-monitoring/schemas) · [Monitor models for training-serving skew with Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/monitor-models-training-serving-skew-vertex-ai)

You are building a deep neural-network classification model from a dataset containing categorical input values. Some columns have a cardinality of more than 10,000 unique values. How should these categorical values be encoded as model input?

options.text: Convert each categorical value into an integer value.
Convert the categorical string data to one-hot hash buckets.
Map the categorical variables into a vector of boolean values.
Convert each categorical value into a run-length encoded string.

questions.explanation:
Hash buckets map high-cardinality categorical strings into a fixed, bounded number of categories, avoiding the very large feature space required by a separate one-hot dimension for every unique value. The resulting buckets can be supplied as one-hot indicator inputs. TensorFlow documents hashed categorical columns specifically as an approach for categorical columns with many values, allowing fewer buckets than actual categories to save space.

**Learn more:** [Classify structured data with feature columns](https://www.tensorflow.org/tutorials/structured_data/feature_columns)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],While executing a model-training pipeline on Vertex Al, you find that the evaluation step is failing with an out-of-memory error. You are using TensorFlow Model Analysis (TFMA) with a standard Evaluator TensorFlow Extended (TFX) pipeline component for that evaluation step. You want to stabilize the pipeline without reducing evaluation quality and while minimizing infrastructure overhead. What should you do?

options.text: Include the flag -runner=DataflowRunner in beam_pipeline_args to run the evaluation step on Dataflow.
Move the evaluation step out of your pipeline and run it on custom Compute Engine VMs with sufficient memory.
Migrate your pipeline to Kubeflow hosted on Google Kubernetes Engine, and specify the appropriate node parameters for the evaluation step.
Add tfma.MetricsSpec () to limit the number of metrics in the evaluation step.

questions.explanation:
The TFX Evaluator uses TFMA, and TFMA uses Apache Beam for scalable evaluation processing. Configuring `beam_pipeline_args` with `--runner=DataflowRunner` runs that Beam work on managed, distributed Dataflow resources, preserving the existing evaluation metrics and analysis while avoiding self-managed VM or Kubernetes infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Apache Beam and TFX](https://www.tensorflow.org/tfx/guide/beam) · [The Evaluator TFX Pipeline Component](https://www.tensorflow.org/tfx/guide/evaluator.md)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work with a data engineering team that has built a pipeline to clean your dataset and store it in a Cloud Storage bucket. You have created an ML model and want to use this data to refresh the model as soon as new data becomes available. As part of your CI/CD workflow, you want to automatically run a Kubeflow Pipelines training job on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). How should you design this workflow?

options.text: Configure your pipeline with Dataflow, which saves the files in Cloud Storage. After the file is saved, start the training job on a GKE cluster.
Use App Engine to create a lightweight python client that continuously polls Cloud Storage for new files. As soon as a file arrives, initiate the training job.

Configure a Cloud Storage trigger to send a message to a Pub/Sub topic when a new file is available in a storage bucket. Use a Pub/Sub-triggered Cloud Function to start the training job on a GKE cluster.

Use Cloud Scheduler to schedule jobs at a regular interval. For the first step of the job, check the timestamp of objects in your Cloud Storage bucket. If there are no new files since the last run, abort the job.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage object-change notifications can publish a message to a Pub/Sub topic when a new file is available. A Pub/Sub-triggered Cloud Function provides an event-driven mechanism to invoke the Kubeflow Pipelines training job on GKE as soon as that event occurs, without continuous polling or scheduled timestamp checks.

**Learn more:** [Pub/Sub notifications for Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/pubsub-notifications) · [Trigger a pipeline run with Pub/Sub](https://cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/pipelines/trigger-pubsub)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You trained a model on a dataset that required computationally costly preprocessing operations. You must perform the same preprocessing at prediction time. The model is deployed on AI Platform for high-throughput online prediction. Which architecture should you use?

options.text: Validate the accuracy of the model that you trained on preprocessed data. Create a new model that uses the raw data and is available in real time. Deploy the new model onto AI Platform for online prediction.

Send incoming prediction requests to a Pub/Sub topic. Transform the incoming data using a Dataflow job. Submit a prediction request to AI Platform using the transformed data. Write the predictions to an outbound Pub/Sub queue.

Stream incoming prediction request data into Cloud Spanner. Create a view to abstract your preprocessing logic. Query the view every second for new records. Submit a prediction request to AI Platform using the transformed data. Write the predictions to an outbound Pub/Sub queue.

Send incoming prediction requests to a Pub/Sub topic. Set up a Cloud Function that is triggered when messages are published to the Pub/Sub topic. Implement your preprocessing logic in the Cloud Function. Submit a prediction request to AI Platform using the transformed data. Write the predictions to an outbound Pub/Sub queue.

questions.explanation:
A Pub/Sub-to-Dataflow streaming pipeline can buffer and scale incoming requests while Dataflow applies the same computationally expensive transformations used for training before sending the transformed instances for prediction. Dataflow supports scalable streaming data processing and ML inference pipelines, making it appropriate for high-throughput preprocessing workloads.

**Learn more:** [About Dataflow ML](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/machine-learning/ml-about) · [Read from Pub/Sub to Dataflow](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/streaming-with-cloud-pubsub)

As the lead ML Engineer at your company, you are responsible for building ML models that digitize scanned customer forms. You developed a TensorFlow model that converts scanned images to text and stores the results in Cloud Storage. You need to run your ML model on the aggregated data collected at the end of every day with minimal manual intervention. What should you do?

options.text: Use the batch prediction functionality of AI Platform.
Create a serving pipeline in Compute Engine for prediction.
Use Cloud Functions for prediction each time a new data point is ingested.
Deploy the model on AI Platform and create a version of it for online inference.

questions.explanation:
AI Platform batch prediction runs asynchronous inference jobs against accumulated input data, including data in Cloud Storage. This matches a daily, high-volume offline workload and avoids the operational overhead of building a custom serving system or using real-time online inference. [gcloud ai-platform jobs submit prediction](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/ai-platform/jobs/submit/prediction)

**Learn more:** [gcloud ai-platform jobs submit prediction](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/ai-platform/jobs/submit/prediction)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a bank that has strict data-governance requirements. You recently implemented a custom model to detect fraudulent transactions. You want the training code to download internal data through an API endpoint hosted in your project’s network. You need the data to be accessed as securely as possible while reducing the risk of data exfiltration. What should you do?

options.text: Enable VPC Service Controls for peerings, and add Vertex AI to a service perimeter.
Create a Cloud Run endpoint as a proxy to the data. Use Identity and Access Management (IAM) authentication to secure access to the endpoint from the training job.
Configure VPC Peering with Vertex AI, and specify the network of the training job.
Download the data to a Cloud Storage bucket before calling the training job.

questions.explanation:
VPC Service Controls creates a security perimeter around supported Google Cloud services, including Vertex AI, and controls ingress and egress across that boundary. This reduces the risk that sensitive training data can be copied to unauthorized resources, while private connectivity supports access to the internal endpoint.

**Learn more:** [Overview of VPC Service Controls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/overview) · [Supported products and limitations for VPC Service Controls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/supported-products)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization’s call center asks you to build a model that analyzes customer sentiment for every call. The call center receives more than one million calls each day, and the data is stored in Cloud Storage. The collected data must remain in the region where the call originated, and no Personally Identifiable Information (PII) may be stored or analyzed. The data science team uses a third-party visualization and access tool that requires a SQL ANSI-2011-compliant interface. You must select components for data processing and analytics. How should the data pipeline be designed?  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783793208659-f6lzpv3o.png)

options.text: 1= Dataflow, 2= BigQuery
1 = Pub/Sub, 2= Datastore
1 = Dataflow, 2 = Cloud SQL
1 = Cloud Function, 2= Cloud SQL

questions.explanation:
Dataflow provides scalable data processing and can be configured to process data in a specified region, supporting locality requirements while invoking Speech-to-Text and de-identifying PII with Cloud Data Loss Prevention before persisting analytics data. BigQuery is designed for large-scale analytics and provides the ANSI-compliant GoogleSQL interface required by the third-party visualization tool.

**Learn more:** [Dataflow regions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/concepts/regional-endpoints) · [Introduction to SQL in BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/introduction-sql)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are an AI engineer working for a popular video-streaming platform. You built a PyTorch classification model to predict customer churn. Each week, the customer-retention team plans to contact customers identified as at risk of churning with personalized offers. You want to deploy the model while minimizing maintenance effort. What should you do?

options.text: Use Vertex AI’s prebuilt containers for prediction. Deploy the container on Cloud Run to generate online predictions.
Use Vertex AI’s prebuilt containers for prediction. Deploy the model on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), and configure the model for batch prediction.
Deploy the model to a Vertex AI endpoint, and configure the model for batch prediction. Schedule the batch prediction to run weekly.
Deploy the model to a Vertex AI endpoint, and configure the model for online prediction. Schedule a job to query this endpoint weekly.

questions.explanation:
Weekly churn scoring is an asynchronous batch-inference workload rather than a real-time prediction requirement. Vertex AI supports managed batch prediction for PyTorch models, allowing a scheduled weekly job to score the customer population without the operational overhead of managing Cloud Run or GKE infrastructure. Online endpoints are intended for real-time inference requests and are unnecessary for this weekly process.

**Learn more:** [PyTorch integration | Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/start/pytorch) · [Create a batch prediction job | Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/samples/aiplatform-create-batch-prediction-job-sample)

questions.question: During exploratory data analysis of a dataset, you discover that an important categorical feature contains 5% null values. You want to reduce the bias that missing values could cause. How should the missing values be handled?

options.text: Remove the rows with missing values, and upsample your dataset by 5%.
Replace the missing values with the feature’s mean.
Replace the missing values with a placeholder category indicating a missing value.
Move the rows with missing values to your validation dataset.

questions.explanation: For a categorical feature, a dedicated placeholder category retains the affected records without inventing a numeric value or changing the dataset split. It also preserves potentially useful information if the fact that a value is missing is predictive.

questions.question: During exploratory data analysis of a dataset, you discover that an important categorical feature contains 5% null values. You want to reduce the bias that missing values could cause. How should the missing values be handled?

options.text: Split incoming traffic to distribute prediction requests among the versions. Monitor the performance of each version using Vertex AI's built-in monitoring tools.

Split incoming traffic among Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) clusters, and use Traffic Director to distribute prediction requests to different versions. Monitor the performance of each version using Cloud Monitoring.
Split incoming traffic to distribute prediction requests among the versions. Monitor the performance of each version using Looker Studio dashboards that compare logged data for each version.
Split incoming traffic among separate Cloud Run instances of deployed models. Monitor the performance of each version using Cloud Monitoring.

questions.explanation:
A public Vertex AI endpoint can split prediction traffic among multiple deployed models by percentage. Vertex AI provides integrated model-monitoring capabilities, avoiding the additional infrastructure and operational setup required for GKE with Traffic Director, separate Cloud Run services, or custom Looker Studio dashboards.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You use Vertex AI to manage your ML models and datasets. options.text: Use Vertex AI TensorBoard to visualize the training metrics of the new model version, and use Data Catalog to manage dataset versioning.
Use Vertex AI Model Monitoring to monitor the performance of the new model version, and use Vertex AI Training to manage dataset versioning.
Use Vertex AI Experiments to track and compare model artifacts and versions, and use Vertex ML Metadata to manage dataset versioning.
Use Vertex AI Experiments to track and compare model artifacts and versions, and use Vertex AI managed datasets to manage dataset versioning.

You are building an ML model on Vertex AI that must satisfy particular interpretability requirements for regulatory compliance. You want to combine model architectures and modeling techniques to maximize both accuracy and interpretability. How should the model be created?

options.text: Use a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based deep learning model architecture, and use local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) for interpretability.
Use a recurrent neural network (RNN)-based deep learning model architecture, and use integrated gradients for interpretability.
Use a boosted decision tree-based model architecture, and use SHAP values for interpretability.
Use a long short-term memory (LSTM)-based model architecture, and use local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) for interpretability.

questions.explanation:
Boosted decision trees commonly achieve strong predictive performance on tabular data while remaining more interpretable than deep neural networks. SHAP values provide consistent feature-attribution explanations for individual predictions and can be aggregated to describe model-wide feature influence, making them well suited to regulatory interpretability needs. Vertex Explainable AI documents Shapley-based attribution as suitable for non-differentiable models such as tree ensembles.

**Learn more:** [Vertex Explainable AI overview](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/explainable-ai/overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your data science team must quickly experiment with different features, model architectures, and hyperparameters. They need to track accuracy metrics across the experiments and query those metrics over time through an API. What should they use to track and report their experiments while minimizing manual effort?

options.text: Use Kubeflow Pipelines to execute the experiments. Export the metrics file, and query the results using the Kubeflow Pipelines API.
Use AI Platform Training to execute the experiments. Write the accuracy metrics to BigQuery, and query the results using the BigQuery API.
Use AI Platform Training to execute the experiments. Write the accuracy metrics to Cloud Monitoring, and query the results using the Monitoring API.
Use AI Platform Notebooks to execute the experiments. Collect the results in a shared Google Sheets file, and query the results using the Google Sheets API.

questions.explanation:
Kubeflow Pipelines supports repeatable ML experiment runs and records pipeline-run metadata and metrics emitted by components. Its API can programmatically retrieve pipeline runs and related results, avoiding a separate manual process to export and store accuracy metrics for each experiment.

**Learn more:** [Kubeflow Pipelines API Reference (v2beta1)](https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/components/pipelines/reference/api/kubeflow-pipeline-api-spec/) · [What is Kubeflow and how can it be used?](https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-kubeflow)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a company developing a new video-streaming platform. You have been asked to create a recommendation system that suggests the next video for a user to watch. Following a review by an AI Ethics team, you are approved to begin development. Each video asset in your company’s catalog has useful metadata (for example, content type, release date, and country), but you have no historical user-event data. How should you build the recommendation system for the first version of the product?

options.text: Launch the product without machine learning. Present videos to users alphabetically, and start collecting user event data so you can develop a recommender model in the future.

Launch the product without machine learning. Use simple heuristics based on content metadata to recommend similar videos to users, and start collecting user event data so you can develop a recommender model in the future.
Launch the product with machine learning. Use a publicly available dataset such as MovieLens to train a model using the Recommendations AI, and then apply this trained model to your data.

Launch the product with machine learning. Generate embeddings for each video by training an autoencoder on the content metadata using TensorFlow. Cluster content based on the similarity of these embeddings, and then recommend videos from the same cluster.

questions.explanation:
Without historical interaction data, a personalized machine-learning recommender lacks the behavioral signals needed for training. Catalog metadata can immediately power simple content-based heuristics that recommend similar videos, while newly collected user events create the data foundation for a later recommender model. Google Cloud guidance likewise identifies user events as required for media recommendation apps and recommends recording those events for recommendations.

**Learn more:** [About media user events](https://docs.cloud.google.com/generative-ai-app-builder/docs/media-user-events) · [Recommendations AI modeling](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/recommendations-ai-modeling)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for an international manufacturing organization that ships scientific products worldwide. The instruction manuals for these products must be translated into 15 different languages. Your organization’s leadership team wants to use machine learning to lower the cost of manual human translation and improve translation speed. You need to implement a scalable solution that maximizes accuracy while minimizing operational overhead. You also want to include a process for evaluating and correcting inaccurate translations. What should you do?

options.text: Create a workflow using Cloud Function triggers. Configure a Cloud Function that is triggered when documents are uploaded to an input Cloud Storage bucket. Configure another Cloud Function that translates the documents using the Cloud Translation API, and saves the translations to an output Cloud Storage bucket. Use human reviewers to evaluate the incorrect translations.

Create a Vertex AI pipeline that processes the documents launches, an AutoML Translation training job, evaluates the translations and deploys the model to a Vertex AI endpoint with autoscaling and model monitoring. When there is a predetermined skew between training and live data, re-trigger the pipeline with the latest data.
Use AutoML Translation to train a model. Configure a Translation Hub project, and use the trained model to translate the documents. Use human reviewers to evaluate the incorrect translations.

Use Vertex AI custom training jobs to fine-tune a state-of-the-art open source pretrained model with your data. Deploy the model to a Vertex AI endpoint with autoscaling and model monitoring. When there is a predetermined skew between the training and live data, configure a trigger to run another training job with the latest data.

questions.explanation:
A custom AutoML Translation model can learn the organization’s domain-specific scientific terminology and translation style, improving translation accuracy. Translation Hub provides a managed, scalable document-translation workflow that supports custom AutoML Translation models and human post-editing, allowing reviewers to correct machine-translated content with minimal operational overhead.

**Learn more:** [Translation Hub](https://cloud.google.com/translation-hub) · [Translation Hub pricing](https://cloud.google.com/translation-hub/pricing)

You work for an online retail company that is building a visual search engine. You have configured an end-to-end ML pipeline on Google Cloud to classify whether an image contains your company's product. Anticipating the release of new products soon, you configured retraining in the pipeline so new data can be supplied to your ML models. You also want to use AI Platform's continuous evaluation service to ensure the models maintain high accuracy on your test dataset. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the original test dataset unchanged even if newer products are incorporated into retraining.
Extend your test dataset with images of the newer products when they are introduced to retraining.
Replace your test dataset with images of the newer products when they are introduced to retraining.
Update your test dataset with images of the newer products when your evaluation metrics drop below a pre-decided threshold.

questions.explanation:
A test dataset should represent the full range of data the model will encounter in production. When newly introduced products are added to retraining data, held-out images of those products must be added to the test dataset as well, while retaining existing examples, so evaluation measures accuracy across both established and new products. Google Cloud documentation states that the test set supplies final evaluation metrics for image models and that each data split should reflect the range of data used for predictions.

**Learn more:** [About data splits for AutoML models](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/general/ml-use)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are an ML engineer at a retail company. You have developed a model that predicts which coupon to offer an ecommerce customer at checkout, based on the items in their cart.  
  
When a customer reaches checkout, your serving pipeline, hosted on Google Cloud, joins the customer’s current cart with a row in a BigQuery table containing the customer’s historic purchase behavior and uses this as the model input. The web team reports that the model returns predictions too slowly to load the coupon offer along with the rest of the web page.  
  
How should you accelerate the model’s predictions?

options.text: Attach an NVIDIA P100 GPU to your deployed model’s instance.
Use a low latency database for the customers’ historic purchase behavior.
Deploy your model to more instances behind a load balancer to distribute traffic.
Create a materialized view in BigQuery with the necessary data for predictions.

questions.explanation:
Online prediction requires low-latency retrieval of the input features. Historical purchase behavior should be served from a low-latency database or online feature-serving store instead of being joined from BigQuery on every checkout request. Google Cloud guidance specifically recommends a low-latency, scalable feature-serving solution for online predictions, while BigQuery remains appropriate for offline feature storage and analytics.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for implementing machine learning on Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/ml-on-gcp-best-practices) · [Feature serving](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/feature-serving)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have recently trained an XGBoost model on tabular data. You intend to expose the model for internal use as an HTTP microservice. After deployment, you anticipate a small number of incoming requests. You want to productionize the model with the least effort and latency. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy the model to BigQuery ML by using CREATE MODEL with the BOOSTED_TREE_REGRESSOR statement, and invoke the BigQuery API from the microservice.
Build a Flask-based app. Package the app in a custom container on Vertex AI, and deploy it to Vertex AI Endpoints.
Build a Flask-based app. Package the app in a Docker image, and deploy it to Google Kubernetes Engine in Autopilot mode.
Use a prebuilt XGBoost Vertex container to create a model, and deploy it to Vertex AI Endpoints.

questions.explanation:
Vertex AI provides prebuilt XGBoost prediction containers and supports online predictions through deployed Vertex AI Endpoints. This managed serving path avoids building a Flask application, maintaining a custom container, and operating Kubernetes, while serving real-time HTTP prediction requests with minimal deployment effort.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a hotel and have a dataset containing customers’ written comments, scanned from paper-based customer feedback forms and stored as PDF files. Every form uses the same layout. You need to rapidly predict an overall satisfaction score from the customer comments on each form. How should you accomplish this task?

options.text: Use the Vision API to parse the text from each PDF file. Use the Natural Language API analyzeSentiment feature to infer overall satisfaction scores.
Use the Vision API to parse the text from each PDF file. Use the Natural Language API analyzeEntitySentiment feature to infer overall satisfaction scores.
Uptrain a Document AI custom extractor to parse the text in the comments section of each PDF file. Use the Natural Language API analyzeSentiment feature to infer overall satisfaction scores.
Uptrain a Document AI custom extractor to parse the text in the comments section of each PDF file. Use the Natural Language API analyzeEntitySentiment feature to infer overall satisfaction scores.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Vision API can perform OCR on scanned PDF documents using document text detection. Cloud Natural Language API `analyzeSentiment` produces a document-level sentiment score that represents the overall opinion expressed in a comment. Entity sentiment is intended for sentiment associated with specific entities, not an overall satisfaction measure; custom extraction training is not required for this OCR-and-document-sentiment workflow.

**Learn more:** [Detect text in files (PDF/TIFF)](https://cloud.google.com/vision/docs/pdf) · [Analyzing Sentiment](https://cloud.google.com/natural-language/docs/analyzing-sentiment)

You have been asked to develop a solution that classifies incoming calls by product so requests can be routed more quickly to the appropriate support team. The calls have already been transcribed by using the Speech-to-Text API. You want to minimize data preprocessing and development time. How should you build the model?

options.text: Use the AI Platform Training built-in algorithms to create a custom model.
Use AutoMlL Natural Language to extract custom entities for classification.
Use the Cloud Natural Language API to extract custom entities for classification.
Build a custom model to identify the product keywords from the transcribed calls, and then run the keywords through a classification algorithm.

questions.explanation:
AutoML Natural Language custom entity extraction trains a managed model to recognize domain-specific entities, such as the company’s product names, directly in transcribed call text. This avoids the feature engineering and custom model development required by AI Platform training or a keyword-based pipeline. The pretrained Cloud Natural Language API can analyze predefined entity types, but it does not create custom entity models.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Natural Language documentation](https://cloud.google.com/natural-language/docs) · [Cloud Natural Language product overview](https://cloud.google.com/natural-language)

Import the model into Vertex AI. On Vertex AI Pipelines, create a pipeline that uses theDataflowPvthonJobOp and the ModelBatchPredictOp components.

questions.explanation:
Vertex AI batch prediction is designed for asynchronous, accumulated inference workloads and runs directly against a model without requiring deployment to an endpoint. questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You trained a model using data that was batch-preprocessed in a Dataflow pipeline. Your use case needs real-time inference. You want to make sure the data-preprocessing logic is applied consistently during training and serving. What should you do?

options.text: Perform data validation to ensure that the input data to the pipeline is the same format as the input data to the endpoint.
Refactor the transformation code in the batch data pipeline so that it can be used outside of the pipeline. Use the same code in the endpoint.
Refactor the transformation code in the batch data pipeline so that it can be used outside of the pipeline. Share this code with the end users of the endpoint.
Batch the real-time requests by using a time window and then use the Dataflow pipeline to preprocess the batched requests. Send the preprocessed requests to the endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Training and serving must use the same feature-transformation implementation so inference inputs have the identical representation the model learned from. Extracting the batch pipeline’s transformation logic into reusable code and using it in the serving endpoint prevents training-serving skew. Google Cloud documents Dataflow ML preprocessing transforms and supports inference in batch and streaming pipelines.

**Learn more:** [Dataflow ML](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/machine-learning)

questions.question:
You built and manage a production system responsible for predicting sales numbers. Model accuracy is crucial because the production model must keep pace with market changes. Since deployment to production, the model has not changed; however, its accuracy has steadily declined.  
  
What issue is most likely causing the steady decline in model accuracy?

options.text: Poor data quality
Lack of model retraining
Too few layers in the model for capturing information
Incorrect data split ratio during model training, evaluation, validation, and test

questions.explanation: As market conditions change, the relationship between input data and sales outcomes can drift. A production model that is not retrained on current data becomes stale, so its predictive accuracy can progressively deteriorate.

You are developing a linear regression model in BigQuery ML to predict a customer's likelihood of purchasing your company's products. The model uses a city-name variable as a key predictive component. To train and serve the model, the data must be arranged in columns. You want to prepare the data with the least amount of coding while retaining the predictive variables. What should you do?

options.text: Use TensorFlow to create a categorical variable with a vocabulary list. Create the vocabulary file, and upload it as part of your model to BigQuery ML.
Create a new view with BigQuery that does not include a column with city information
Use Cloud Data Fusion to assign each city to a region labeled as 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5, and then use that number to represent the city in the model.
Use Dataprep to transform the state column using a one-hot encoding method, and make each city a column with binary values.

questions.explanation:
One-hot encoding converts each categorical city value into its own binary feature, preserving the information in the city predictor while avoiding a false numeric or ordinal relationship between cities. BigQuery ML uses one-hot encoding for non-numeric features in applicable linear models, and low-code data-preparation tooling can create the required binary columns consistently for training and serving.

**Learn more:** [Automatic feature preprocessing | BigQuery | Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/auto-preprocessing) · [The CREATE MODEL statement for generalized linear models | BigQuery | Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-create-glm)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a retail company that uses a regression model built with BigQuery ML to predict product sales. The model serves online predictions. Recently, you developed a new model version that uses a different architecture (custom model). Initial analysis showed that both models are performing as expected. You want to deploy the new model version to production and monitor its performance over the next two months. You need to minimize the impact on existing and future model users. How should you deploy the model?

options.text: Import the new model to the same Vertex AI Model Registry as a different version of the existing model. Deploy the new model to the same Vertex AI endpoint as the existing model, and use traffic splitting to route 95% of production traffic to the BigQuery ML model and 5% of production traffic to the new model.

Import the new model to the same Vertex AI Model Registry as the existing model. Deploy the models to one Vertex AI endpoint. Route 95% of production traffic to the BigQuery ML model and 5% of production traffic to the new model.
Import the new model to the same Vertex AI Model Registry as the existing model. Deploy each model to a separate Vertex AI endpoint.
Deploy the new model to a separate Vertex AI endpoint. Create a Cloud Run service that routes the prediction requests to the corresponding endpoints based on the input feature values.

questions.explanation:
Vertex AI endpoints can host multiple deployed models and route a specified percentage of endpoint traffic to each one. Deploying both versions to the existing endpoint with a 95%/5% traffic split implements a low-impact canary rollout: most users continue receiving predictions from the established BigQuery ML model while the custom model receives representative production traffic for monitoring. During exploratory analysis of a dataset, you find that categorical feature A has significant predictive power but is occasionally missing. What should you do?

options.text: Drop feature A if more than 15% of values are missing. Otherwise, use feature A as-is.
Compute the mode of feature A and then use it to replace the missing values in feature A.
Replace the missing values with the values of the feature with the highest Pearson correlation with feature A.
Add an additional class to categorical feature A for missing values. Create a new binary feature that indicates whether feature A is missing.

questions.explanation: Retain predictive categorical features and represent missing values explicitly. Assigning missing entries to a separate category preserves any signal associated with missingness, while a binary missingness indicator allows a model to use that condition directly rather than conflating missing values with the most common observed category.

You are an ML engineer at a mobile gaming company. A data scientist on your team has recently trained a TensorFlow model, and you are responsible for deploying it in a mobile application. You find that the current model’s inference latency does not meet production requirements. You must reduce inference time by 50% and are willing to accept a small reduction in model accuracy to achieve the latency requirement. Without training a new model, which model-optimization technique should you try first to reduce latency?

options.text: Weight pruning
Dynamic range quantization
Model distillation
Dimensionality reduction

questions.explanation:
TensorFlow Lite dynamic range quantization is a post-training conversion optimization that reduces weight precision and can use faster quantized computation where supported. TensorFlow documents it as a recommended starting point because it reduces memory use and speeds computation without requiring a representative calibration dataset; its post-training quantization guidance lists dynamic range quantization as providing roughly 2–3× CPU speedup with a small accuracy trade-off.

**Learn more:** [TensorFlow Model Optimization: Post-training quantization](https://www.tensorflow.org/model_optimization/guide/quantization/post_training) · [TensorFlow Lite: Post-training quantization](https://www.tensorflow.org/lite/performance/post_training_quantization)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are testing a built-in distributed XGBoost model in Vertex AI Workbench user-managed notebooks. You use BigQuery to divide your data into training and validation sets with the following queries:  
  
```sql  
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ‘myproject.mydataset.training‘ AS  
(SELECT * FROM ‘myproject.mydataset.mytable‘ WHERE RAND() <= 0.8);  
  
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ‘myproject.mydataset.validation‘ AS  
(SELECT * FROM ‘myproject.mydataset.mytable‘ WHERE RAND() <= 0.2);  
```  
  
After training the model, you obtain an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC ROC) of 0.8. However, after deploying the model to production, you observe that its performance has fallen to an AUC ROC of 0.65. What problem is most likely happening?

options.text: There is training-serving skew in your production environment.
There is not a sufficient amount of training data.
The tables that you created to hold your training and validation records share some records, and you may not be using all the data in your initial table.
The RAND() function generated a number that is less than 0.2 in both instances, so every record in the validation table will also be in the training table.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery RAND() generates a pseudo-random value in the range [0, 1). Because the two table-creation queries call RAND() independently, records may be included in both tables and others may be excluded from both. The overlap leaks training records into validation, inflating the measured validation AUC and making the production performance appear to drop.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery mathematical functions: RAND](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/mathematical_functions#rand)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a bank and have built a custom model that predicts whether a loan application should be flagged for human review. The input features are stored in a BigQuery table. The model performs well, and you intend to deploy it to production.  
  
Because of compliance requirements, the model must provide an explanation for every prediction. You want to add this capability to the model code with minimal effort while providing explanations that are as accurate as possible. What should you do?

options.text: Create an AutoML tabular model by using the BigQuery data with integrated Vertex Explainable AI.
Create a BigQuery ML deep neural network model and use the ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT method with the num_integral_steps parameter.
Upload the custom model to Vertex AI Model Registry and configure feature-based attribution by using sampled Shapley with input baselines.
Update the custom serving container to include sampled Shapley-based explanations in the prediction outputs.

questions.explanation:
Vertex Explainable AI can be configured for a custom model in Vertex AI Model Registry to return per-prediction feature attributions. Sampled Shapley is supported for custom models and is appropriate for tabular classification and regression. Supplying representative input baselines helps produce meaningful, accurate feature attributions without reimplementing explanation logic in the serving container.

**Learn more:** [Vertex AI Explainable AI overview](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/explainable-ai/overview) · [Improve feature-based explanations](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/explainable-ai/improving-explanations)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have been asked to productionize a proof-of-concept ML model created with Keras. The model was trained in a Jupyter notebook on a data scientist’s local machine. The notebook includes one cell for data validation and another cell for model analysis.  
  
You need to orchestrate the steps in the notebook and automate their execution for weekly retraining. You expect substantially more training data in the future. You want the solution to use managed services while minimizing cost. What should you do?

options.text: Move the Jupyter notebook to a Notebooks instance on the largest N2 machine type, and schedule the execution of the steps in the Notebooks instance using Cloud Scheduler.

Write the code as a TensorFlow Extended (TFX) pipeline orchestrated with Vertex AI Pipelines. Use standard TFX components for data validation and model analysis, and use Vertex AI Pipelines for model retraining.
Rewrite the steps in the Jupyter notebook as an Apache Spark job, and schedule the execution of the job on ephemeral Dataproc clusters using Cloud Scheduler.
Extract the steps contained in the Jupyter notebook as Python scripts, wrap each script in an Apache Airflow BashOperator, and run the resulting directed acyclic graph (DAG) in Cloud Composer.

questions.explanation:
TensorFlow Extended (TFX) provides production ML pipeline components, including TensorFlow Data Validation for detecting data anomalies and TensorFlow Model Analysis for evaluating and analyzing models. Vertex AI Pipelines is a serverless managed orchestration service that runs TFX pipelines, supports recurring pipeline runs, and avoids maintaining dedicated notebook, Spark, or Airflow infrastructure while accommodating larger training workloads.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Vertex AI Pipelines](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/pipelines/introduction) · [Architecture for MLOps using TensorFlow Extended, Vertex AI Pipelines, and Cloud Build](https://cloud.google.com/solutions/machine-learning/architecture-for-mlops-using-tfx-kubeflow-pipelines-and-cloud-build)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a model to recognize traffic signs in images extracted from videos recorded from a vehicle dashboard. You have a dataset of 100,000 images, each cropped to display one of ten different traffic signs. The images are labeled for model training and stored in a Cloud Storage bucket. You need to be able to tune the model in every training run. How should you train the model?

options.text: Train a model for object detection by using Vertex AI AutoML.
Train a model for image classification by using Vertex AI AutoML.
Develop the model training code for object detection, and train a model by using Vertex AI custom training.
Develop the model training code for image classification, and train a model by using Vertex AI custom training.

questions.explanation:
Because every cropped image contains a single labeled traffic sign, the prediction task is image classification, not object detection; object detection requires annotations that locate objects, such as bounding boxes. Custom training lets the training code accept and use hyperparameters, and Vertex AI hyperparameter-tuning jobs run custom-job trials with different parameter values.

**Learn more:** [Train an image classification model](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/image-data/classification/train-model) · [HyperparameterTuningJob REST resource](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.hyperparameterTuningJobs)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a binary-classification ML algorithm to identify whether an image of a classified scanned document includes a company’s logo. In the dataset, 96% of examples lack the logo, making the dataset highly skewed. Which metric would give you the greatest confidence in the model?

options.text: Precision
Recall
RMSE
F1 score

questions.explanation:
The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, so it assesses both the correctness of logo detections and the model’s ability to find actual logos. This balanced positive-class measure is more informative than either precision or recall alone for a highly imbalanced binary classification dataset. RMSE is a regression metric.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SageMaker AI metrics reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/canvas-metrics.html) · [Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels: Metrics for evaluating your model](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rekognition/latest/customlabels-dg/im-metrics-use.html)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to run batch prediction on 100 million records in a BigQuery table by using a custom TensorFlow DNN regressor model, then save the prediction results in a BigQuery table. You want to minimize the effort needed to build this inference pipeline. What should you do?

options.text: Import the TensorFlow model with BigQuery ML, and run the ml.predict function.
Use the TensorFlow BigQuery reader to load the data, and use the BigQuery API to write the results to BigQuery.
Create a Dataflow pipeline to convert the data in BigQuery to TFRecords. Run a batch inference on Vertex AI Prediction, and write the results to BigQuery.
Load the TensorFlow SavedModel in a Dataflow pipeline. Use the BigQuery I/O connector with a custom function to perform the inference within the pipeline, and write the results to BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery ML can import a TensorFlow SavedModel and use `ML.PREDICT` directly against BigQuery data. The SQL query output can be materialized into a BigQuery table, so no separate Dataflow pipeline, TFRecord conversion, or custom read/write code is required.

**Learn more:** [Make predictions with imported TensorFlow models](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/making-predictions-with-imported-tensorflow-models) · [The ML.PREDICT function](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-predict)
