You work for a company that records live video footage of checkout areas in its retail stores. You need to use that live video footage to build a model that detects, in near real time, how many customers are waiting for service. You want to implement the solution quickly and with minimal effort. How should you build the model?

options.text: Use the Vertex AI Vision Occupancy Analytics model.
Use the Vertex AI Vision Person/vehicle detector model.
Train an AutoML object detection model on an annotated dataset by using Vertex AutoML.
Train a Seq2Seq+ object detection model on an annotated dataset by using Vertex AutoML.

questions.explanation:
The Vertex AI Vision Occupancy Analytics model is prebuilt for counting people or vehicles in user-defined active zones in a video stream. A checkout waiting area can be defined as an active zone, enabling near-real-time customer counts without creating an annotated dataset or training a custom object-detection model.

**Learn more:** [Occupancy analytics guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vision-ai/docs/occupancy-analytics-model)

questions.question: You are developing an ML model that detects anomalies in real-time sensor data. You will use Pub/Sub to process incoming requests and want to store the results for analytics and visualization. How should the pipeline be configured?

options.text: 1 = Dataflow, 2 = AI Platform, 3 = BigQuery
1 = DataProc, 2 = AutoML, 3 = Cloud Bigtable
1 = BigQuery, 2 = AutoML, 3 = Cloud Functions
1 = BigQuery, 2 = AI Platform, 3 = Cloud Storage

questions.explanation:
Dataflow provides managed, low-latency stream processing for Pub/Sub data and supports real-time ML analysis. AI Platform serves online predictions from a trained model, and BigQuery stores the resulting data for analytical queries and visualization.\
\
**Learn more:** [Dataflow overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/overview) · [gcloud ai-platform predict](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/ai-platform/predict)

questions.question: You are developing an ML model that detects anomalies in real-time sensor data. You will use Pub/Sub to process incoming requests and want to store the results for analytics and visualization. How should the pipeline be configured?

options.text: Remove the data transformation step from your pipeline.
Containerize the PySpark transformation step, and add it to your pipeline.
Add a ContainerOp to your pipeline that spins a Dataproc cluster, runs a transformation, and then saves the transformed data in Cloud Storage.
Deploy Apache Spark at a separate node pool in a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster. Add a ContainerOp to your pipeline that invokes a corresponding transformation job for this Spark instance.

questions.explanation:
The existing preprocessing relies on PySpark reading a Hive table over Parquet, which needs a managed Spark/Hadoop environment; the cleanest way to parameterize this inside Kubeflow Pipelines on Google Cloud is to add a ContainerOp that spins up a Dataproc cluster, runs the transformation, and writes the result to Cloud Storage (C). This keeps the transformation as a reproducible, parameterized pipeline step while offloading the heavy Spark work to the purpose-built managed service. Simply containerizing the PySpark step (B) would require you to bundle and manage a Spark runtime and Hive connectivity yourself, which is far more brittle than using Dataproc. Removing the transformation (A) loses required preprocessing, and standing up a separate long-lived Spark node pool in GKE (D) is unnecessary operational overhead compared with ephemeral Dataproc.

**Learn more:** [Kubeflow Dataproc components](https://github.com/arrikto/kubeflow-pipelines/blob/master/components/gcp/dataproc/submit_hive_job/README.md) · [Preprocessing in Kubeflow with Dataproc](https://medium.com/@vignesh093/running-preprocessing-and-ml-workflow-in-kubeflow-with-google-dataproc-84103a9ef67e)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an ML model to predict stock-market trends from a broad set of factors. During data exploration, you observe that some features span a large range. You want to make sure features with the greatest magnitude do not cause the model to overfit. What should you do?

options.text: Standardize the data by transforming it with a logarithmic function.
Apply a principal component analysis (PCA) to minimize the effect of any particular feature.
Use a binning strategy to replace the magnitude of each feature with the appropriate bin number.
Normalize the data by scaling it to have values between 0 and 1.

questions.explanation:
Min-max normalization rescales each numeric feature to a common range of 0 to 1, preventing features with wider numeric ranges from receiving disproportionate influence merely because of their magnitude. Feature scaling helps a model learn appropriate weights across features with substantially different ranges.

**Learn more:** [Numerical data: Normalization](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/numerical-data/normalization)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are an ML engineer at a bank. You developed a binary-classification model with AutoML Tables to predict whether a customer will make loan payments on time. Its output is used to approve or reject loan applications. One customer's loan application was rejected by the model, and the bank's risk department asks for the reasons that contributed to that decision. What should you do?

options.text: Use local feature importance from the predictions.
Use the correlation with target values in the data summary page.
Use the feature importance percentages in the model evaluation page.
Vary features independently to identify the threshold per feature that changes the classification.

questions.explanation:
Local feature importance supplies feature attributions for an individual inference, showing how much each input feature contributed to that specific classification result. Global feature importance, target correlation, and manual feature variation do not directly explain the individual rejection.

**Learn more:** [Feature attributions for classification and regression](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/tabular-data/classification-explanations) · [Get online inferences for AutoML models](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/tabular-data/classification-regression/get-online-predictions)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You recently deployed a Vertex AI Pipelines pipeline that trains and pushes a model to a Vertex AI endpoint for serving real-time traffic. You need to keep experimenting with and iterating on your pipeline to improve model performance. You plan to use Cloud Build for CI/CD. You want to deploy new pipelines to production quickly and easily while minimizing the risk that new pipeline implementations will fail in production. What should you do?

options.text: Set up a CI/CD pipeline that builds and tests your source code. If the tests are successful, use the Google. Cloud console to upload the built container to Artifact Registry and upload the compiled pipeline to Vertex AI Pipelines.

Set up a CI/CD pipeline that builds your source code and then deploys built artifacts into a pre-production environment. Run unit tests in the pre-production environment. If the tests are successful deploy the pipeline to production.

Set up a CI/CD pipeline that builds and tests your source code and then deploys built artifacts into a pre-production environment. After a successful pipeline run in the pre-production environment, deploy the pipeline to production.

Set up a CI/CD pipeline that builds and tests your source code and then deploys built artifacts into a pre-production environment. After a successful pipeline run in the pre-production environment, rebuild the source code and deploy the artifacts to production.

questions.explanation:
A robust ML CI/CD process builds and tests source code, deploys the resulting immutable artifacts to a pre-production environment, validates them by successfully running the pipeline, and promotes those same artifacts to production. This provides end-to-end validation before release and avoids the inconsistency risk of rebuilding artifacts after pre-production testing.

**Learn more:** [Architecture for MLOps using TensorFlow Extended, Vertex AI Pipelines, and Cloud Build](https://cloud.google.com/solutions/machine-learning/architecture-for-mlops-using-tfx-kubeflow-pipelines-and-cloud-build)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a natural language processing model that analyzes customer feedback to classify experiences as positive, negative, or neutral. During testing, you find that the model shows significant bias against certain demographic groups, resulting in skewed analysis outcomes. You want to resolve this issue in accordance with Google's responsible AI practices. What should you do?

options.text: Use Vertex AI's model evaluation lo assess bias in the model's predictions, and use post-processing to adjust outputs for identified demographic discrepancies.
Implement a more complex model architecture that can capture nuanced patterns in language to reduce bias.
Audit the training dataset to identify underrepresented groups and augment the dataset with additional samples before retraining the model.
Use Vertex Explainable AI to generate explanations and systematically adjust the predictions to address identified biases.

questions.explanation:
Training data that underrepresents demographic groups can produce systematically unfair model performance for those groups. Auditing the data, adding representative samples, and retraining mitigates data-level bias at its source. Vertex AI fairness evaluation distinguishes data bias that can be detected before training from model bias detected after training.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to model evaluation for fairness](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/evaluation/intro-evaluation-fairness) · [Data bias metrics for Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/evaluation/data-bias-metrics)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a model to identify fraudulent credit card transactions. You must prioritize detection because failing to detect even one fraudulent transaction could severely affect the credit card holder. You used AutoML to train a model using users' profile information and credit card transaction data. After training the initial model, you find that it fails to detect many fraudulent transactions. How can you increase the number of fraudulent transactions detected?

options.text: Add more non-fraudulent examples to the training set.
Reduce the maximum number of node hours for training.
Increase the probability threshold to classify a fraudulent transaction.
Decrease the probability threshold to classify a fraudulent transaction.

questions.explanation:
Reducing the probability threshold causes more transactions to be classified as fraudulent, increasing recall and reducing false negatives. This trade-off can also increase false positives, but it is appropriate when missing fraud has the greater cost. Google Cloud documents that higher confidence thresholds increase precision while decreasing recall; therefore, lowering the threshold increases recall.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to tabular data | Vertex AI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/tabular-data/tabular101) · [Evaluate AutoML classification models | Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/text-data/classification/evaluate-model?hl=pt-br)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are an ML engineer tasked with designing and implementing training pipelines for ML models. You must create an end-to-end training pipeline for a TensorFlow model. The TensorFlow model will train on several terabytes of structured data. The pipeline must include data-quality checks before training and model-quality checks after training but before deployment. You want to minimize development time and infrastructure-maintenance requirements. How should you build and orchestrate the training pipeline?

options.text: Create the pipeline using Kubeflow Pipelines domain-specific language (DSL) and predefined Google Cloud components. Orchestrate the pipeline using Vertex AI Pipelines.
Create the pipeline using TensorFlow Extended (TFX) and standard TFX components. Orchestrate the pipeline using Vertex AI Pipelines.

Create the pipeline using Kubeflow Pipelines domain-specific language (DSL) and predefined Google Cloud components. Orchestrate the pipeline using Kubeflow Pipelines deployed on Google Kubernetes Engine.
Create the pipeline using TensorFlow Extended (TFX) and standard TFX components. Orchestrate the pipeline using Kubeflow Pipelines deployed on Google Kubernetes Engine.

questions.explanation:
TensorFlow Extended (TFX) supplies standard components for production TensorFlow workflows, including data validation before training and model evaluation/validation that can gate deployment. Vertex AI Pipelines is a managed, serverless orchestrator for TFX or Kubeflow pipelines, so it avoids the operational overhead of deploying and maintaining Kubeflow Pipelines on Google Kubernetes Engine.

**Learn more:** [Vertex AI Pipelines introduction](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/pipelines/introduction) · [Architecture for MLOps using TensorFlow Extended, Vertex AI Pipelines, and Cloud Build](https://cloud.google.com/solutions/machine-learning/architecture-for-mlops-using-tfx-kubeflow-pipelines-and-cloud-build)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to deploy a scikit-leam classification model into production. The model must serve requests 24/7, and the production application is expected to receive millions of requests per second from 8 am to 7 pm. You need to minimize deployment costs. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy an online Vertex AI prediction endpoint. Set the max replica count to 1
Deploy an online Vertex AI prediction endpoint. Set the max replica count to 100
Deploy an online Vertex AI prediction endpoint with one GPU per replica. Set the max replica count to 1
Deploy an online Vertex AI prediction endpoint with one GPU per replica. Set the max replica count to 100

questions.explanation:
A CPU-based online Vertex AI endpoint with a maximum of 100 replicas can autoscale to serve very high peak demand while reducing the number of active replicas as demand declines. scikit-learn classification inference typically does not need GPUs, so GPU-equipped replicas would add unnecessary cost. A maximum of one replica cannot provide capacity for millions of requests per second.

**Learn more:** [Autoscale inference nodes](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/autoscaling) · [Get online inferences from a custom trained model](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/get-online-predictions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work at a biotech startup that is experimenting with deep-learning ML models based on the properties of biological organisms. Your team frequently conducts early-stage experiments with new ML-model architectures and writes custom TensorFlow ops in C++.  
  
You train your models on large datasets with large batch sizes. Your typical batch size is 1024 examples, and each example is approximately 1 MB in size. The average size of a network, including all weights and embeddings, is 20 GB. What hardware should you select for your models?

options.text: A cluster with 2 n1-highcpu-64 machines, each with 8 NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPUs (128 GB GPU memory in total), and a n1-highcpu-64 machine with 64 vCPUs and 58 GB RAM
A cluster with 2 a2-megagpu-16g machines, each with 16 NVIDIA Tesla A100 GPUs (640 GB GPU memory in total), 96 vCPUs, and 1.4 TB RAM
A cluster with an n1-highcpu-64 machine with a v2-8 TPU and 64 GB RAM
A cluster with 4 n1-highcpu-96 machines, each with 96 vCPUs and 86 GB RAM

questions.explanation:
GPU-based Compute Engine instances are appropriate for large models and large effective batch sizes, and they avoid the Cloud TPU operation-compatibility limitations that can affect custom TensorFlow operations. A2 `a2-megagpu-16g` machines provide 16 NVIDIA A100 GPUs and 640 GB of GPU memory per machine, offering the accelerator capacity needed for this large-scale training workload.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Cloud TPU](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tpu/docs/intro-to-tpu) · [GPU machine types](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a large retailer and have been asked to segment customers based on their purchasing habits. The purchase history for all customers has been uploaded to BigQuery. You suspect there may be several distinct customer segments, but you are unsure how many there are and do not yet understand the similarities in their behavior. You want to find the most efficient solution. What should you do?

options.text: Create a k-means clustering model using BigQuery ML. Allow BigQuery to automatically optimize the number of clusters.
Create a new dataset in Dataprep that references your BigQuery table. Use Dataprep to identify similarities within each column.

Use the Data Labeling Service to label each customer record in BigQuery. Train a model on your labeled data using AutoML Tables. Review the evaluation metrics to understand whether there is an underlying pattern in the data.

Get a list of the customer segments from your company’s Marketing team. Use the Data Labeling Service to label each customer record in BigQuery according to the list. Analyze the distribution of labels in your dataset using Data Studio.

questions.explanation:
K-means is an unsupervised clustering method for grouping similar records when no segment labels are available. BigQuery ML supports K-means specifically for data segmentation, including identifying customer segments, and supports tuning the number of clusters using the Davies–Bouldin index.

**Learn more:** [The CREATE MODEL statement for K-means models](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-create-kmeans) · [Clustering overview](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/clustering-overview)

options.text: Configure one a2-highgpu-1g instance with an NVIDIA A100 GPU with 80 GB of RAM. Use float32 precision during model training.
Configure one a2-highgpu-1g instance with an NVIDIA A100 GPU with 80 GB of RAM. Use bfloat16 quantization during model training.
Configure four n1-standard-16 instances, each with one NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU with 16 GB of RAM. Use float32 precision during model training.
Configure four n1-standard-16 instances, each with one NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU with 16 GB of RAM. Use floar16 quantization during model training.

questions.explanation:
An NVIDIA A100 supports bfloat16 mixed-precision training through Tensor Cores, providing substantially greater training throughput than T4 GPUs while reducing memory use relative to float32. Its documented mixed-precision Tensor Core performance is 312 TFLOPS, compared with 65 TFLOPS for an N1 T4; a single A100 also avoids the communication overhead of distributing training across four separate instances.

**Learn more:** [GPU machine types — Compute Engine](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus)

You work for a large retailer and must build a model to predict customer churn. The company has a dataset containing historical customer data, including customer demographics, purchase history, and website activity. You need to create the model in BigQuery ML and thoroughly assess its performance. What should you do?

options.text: Create a linear regression model in BigQuery ML, and register the model in Vertex AI Model Registry. Use Vertex AI to evaluate the model performance.
Create a logistic regression model in BigQuery ML, and register the model in Vertex AI Model Registry. Use ML.ARIMA_EVALUATE function to evaluate the model performance.
Create a linear regression model in BigQuery ML. Use the ML.EVALUATE function to evaluate the model performance.
Create a logistic regression model in BigQuery ML. Use the ML.CONFUSION_MATRIX function to evaluate the model performance.

questions.explanation:
Customer churn prediction is a classification task, for which BigQuery ML logistic regression is appropriate. `ML.CONFUSION_MATRIX` returns the classification results by expected and predicted label, enabling detailed assessment of correct and incorrect predictions.

**Learn more:** [The ML.CONFUSION_MATRIX function](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-confusion) · [BigQuery ML model evaluation overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/evaluate-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You developed an ML model with AI Platform and want to move it into production. You handle a few thousand queries per second and are encountering latency problems. Incoming requests are handled by a load balancer that distributes them among multiple Kubeflow CPU-only pods running on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).  
  
Your goal is to improve serving latency without changing the underlying infrastructure. What should you do?

options.text: Significantly increase the max_batch_size TensorFlow Serving parameter.
Switch to the tensorflow-model-server-universal version of TensorFlow Serving.
Significantly increase the max_enqueued_batches TensorFlow Serving parameter.
Recompile TensorFlow Serving using the source to support CPU-specific optimizations. Instruct GKE to choose an appropriate baseline minimum CPU platform for serving nodes.

questions.explanation:
CPU-specific TensorFlow Serving builds can use processor instruction-set optimizations that portable binaries leave out for broad compatibility, reducing inference execution time. GKE minimum CPU-platform selection ensures serving nodes provide a compatible CPU feature set. Increasing batch size or queued batches primarily changes batching and queue behavior, which can add waiting time and does not directly make each CPU inference faster.

**Learn more:** [TensorFlow Serving installation and optimized builds](https://www.tensorflow.org/tfx/serving/setup) · [Choose a minimum CPU platform in GKE](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/min-cpu-platform)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a startup with multiple data science workloads. Your compute infrastructure is presently on-premises, and the data science workloads are written natively in PySpark. Your team intends to migrate these data science workloads to Google Cloud.  
  
You need to build a proof of concept that migrates one data science job to Google Cloud. You want to recommend a migration process that involves minimal cost and effort. What should you do first?

options.text: Create a n2-standard-4 VM instance and install Java, Scala, and Apache Spark dependencies on it.
Create a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster with a basic node pool configuration, install Java, Scala, and Apache Spark dependencies on it.
Create a Standard (1 master, 3 workers) Dataproc cluster, and run a Vertex AI Workbench notebook instance on it.
Create a Vertex AI Workbench notebook with instance type n2-standard-4.

questions.explanation:
A standard Dataproc cluster provides a managed Apache Spark environment, avoiding the installation and operation of Java, Scala, and Spark on self-managed Compute Engine or GKE infrastructure. Dataproc supports submitting PySpark jobs directly, and a Vertex AI Workbench notebook can use a remote Spark kernel on a Dataproc cluster. This supplies a suitable distributed runtime for a PySpark proof of concept with substantially less setup effort.

**Learn more:** [Submit a job | Managed Service for Apache Spark](https://docs.cloud.google.com/managed-spark/docs/guides/submit-job) · [Create a Vertex AI Workbench instance enabled for Dataproc Spark](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/workbench/instances/create-dataproc-enabled)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are an ML engineer on an agricultural research team developing a crop-disease detection tool that identifies leaf-rust spots in crop images to determine whether disease is present. These spots can differ in shape and size and correlate with disease severity. You want to build a solution that predicts disease presence and severity with high accuracy. What should you do?

options.text: Create an object detection model that can localize the rust spots.
Develop an image segmentation ML model to locate the boundaries of the rust spots.
Develop a template matching algorithm using traditional computer vision libraries.
Develop an image classification ML model to predict the presence of the disease.

questions.explanation:
Image segmentation assigns labels at the pixel level, allowing precise rust-spot boundaries and areas to be measured. Those measurements capture the variable shape and size associated with disease severity, while object detection generally localizes objects with rectangular bounds and image classification only produces an image-level prediction.

**Learn more:** [Detect multiple objects | Cloud Vision API](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vision/docs/object-localizer)

You work for an organization that operates a cloud-based communications platform combining conventional chat, voice, and video conferencing in one platform. Audio recordings are stored in Cloud Storage. Every recording has an 8 kHz sample rate and lasts longer than one minute.  
  
You need to add a platform feature that automatically transcribes voice-call recordings to text for future uses such as call summarization and sentiment analysis. How should you implement the voice-call transcription feature according to Google-recommended best practices?

options.text: Use the original audio sampling rate, and transcribe the audio by using the Speech-to-Text API with synchronous recognition.
Use the original audio sampling rate, and transcribe the audio by using the Speech-to-Text API with asynchronous recognition.
Upsample the audio recordings to 16 kHz, and transcribe the audio by using the Speech-to-Text API with synchronous recognition.
Upsample the audio recordings to 16 kHz, and transcribe the audio by using the Speech-to-Text API with asynchronous recognition.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Speech-to-Text requires asynchronous recognition for audio longer than 60 seconds, and Cloud Storage is the appropriate input location for such long-running transcription. For audio already recorded as 8 kHz telephony audio, Google recommends sending it at its native sampling rate rather than upsampling it, because resampling cannot restore the missing frequency information.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Speech-to-Text best practices](https://docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/best-practices) · [Cloud Speech-to-Text recognition requests](https://docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/v1/speech-to-text-requests)

You work for a bank and are developing a random forest model to detect fraud. Your dataset contains transactions, with 1% identified as fraudulent. Which data-transformation strategy would most likely improve the classifier's performance?

options.text: Write your data in TFRecords.
Z-normalize all the numeric features.
Oversample the fraudulent transaction 10 times.
Use one-hot encoding on all categorical features.

questions.explanation:
Oversampling the fraudulent minority class increases the number of fraud examples seen during training, reducing the effect of the 99%-to-1% class imbalance and helping the classifier learn patterns associated with fraud. Class imbalance can otherwise lead a model to favor the majority class. [Google Machine Learning Crash Course: Class-imbalanced datasets](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/overfitting/imbalanced-datasets)

**Learn more:** [Google Machine Learning Crash Course: Class-imbalanced datasets](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/overfitting/imbalanced-datasets)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building an ML model that predicts the cost of used automobiles from data such as location, condition, model type, color, and engine/battery efficiency. The data is refreshed every night. Car dealerships will use the model to set appropriate car prices.  
  
You created a Vertex AI pipeline that reads the data, splits it into training/evaluation/test sets, performs feature engineering, trains the model using the training dataset, and validates the model using the evaluation dataset. You need to configure a retraining workflow that minimizes cost. What should you do?

options.text: Compare the training and evaluation losses of the current run. If the losses are similar, deploy the model to a Vertex AI endpoint. Configure a cron job to redeploy the pipeline every night.

Compare the training and evaluation losses of the current run. If the losses are similar, deploy the model to a Vertex AI endpoint with training/serving skew threshold model monitoring. When the model monitoring threshold is triggered redeploy the pipeline.
Compare the results to the evaluation results from a previous run. If the performance improved deploy the model to a Vertex AI endpoint. Configure a cron job to redeploy the pipeline every night.

Compare the results to the evaluation results from a previous run. If the performance improved deploy the model to a Vertex AI endpoint with training/serving skew threshold model monitoring. When the model monitoring threshold is triggered redeploy the pipeline.

questions.explanation:
A candidate model should be deployed only when its evaluation performance improves on the prior model’s evaluation result; training and evaluation losses being similar does not show that it is superior to the incumbent model. Training-serving skew monitoring compares serving feature distributions with the training baseline and alerts when configured thresholds are exceeded. Using that signal to trigger retraining avoids the unnecessary recurring training cost of nightly retraining while responding when production data has materially changed.

**Learn more:** [AI and ML perspective: Operational excellence](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/perspectives/ai-ml/operational-excellence) · [Vertex AI Experiments documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/experiments/intro-vertex-ai-experiments)

Your team has a model deployed to a Vertex AI endpoint. You created a Vertex AI pipeline that automates model training and is triggered by a Cloud Function. You need to prioritize keeping the model current while minimizing retraining costs. How should you configure retraining?

options.text: Configure Pub/Sub to call the Cloud Function when a sufficient amount of new data becomes available
Configure a Cloud Scheduler job that calls the Cloud Function at a predetermined frequency that fits your team’s budget
Enable model monitoring on the Vertex AI endpoint. Configure Pub/Sub to call the Cloud Function when anomalies are detected
Enable model monitoring on the Vertex AI endpoint. Configure Pub/Sub to call the Cloud Function when feature drift is detected

questions.explanation:
Feature drift detection compares production feature distributions with the training baseline and alerts when configured thresholds are exceeded. Triggering the training pipeline only on detected feature drift provides an event-driven retraining process that refreshes the model when its inputs have materially changed, while avoiding unnecessary retraining runs.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/ai-platform/docs?o=7639) · [ModelMonitoringNotificationSpec](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1beta1/ModelMonitoringNotificationSpec)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You trained a model, packaged it in a custom Docker serving container, and deployed it to Vertex AI Model Registry. When you submit a batch prediction job, it fails with the following error: "Error model server never became ready. Please validate that your model file or container configuration are valid."  
  
There are no additional errors in the logs. What should you do?

options.text: Add a logging configuration to your application to emit logs to Cloud Logging
Change the HTTP port in your model’s configuration to the default value of 8080
Change the healthRoute value in your model’s configuration to /healthcheck
Pull the Docker image locally, and use the docker run command to launch it locally. Use the docker logs command to explore the error logs

questions.explanation:
A custom inference container must start successfully and become ready before batch prediction can proceed. Running the image locally and inspecting `docker logs` exposes container startup failures, such as an invalid entrypoint, missing dependency, model-loading failure, or incorrect runtime configuration. Vertex AI custom containers can use a configured port and health route, but neither a fixed port nor a specific `/healthcheck` path is universally required.

**Learn more:** [Use a custom container for inference](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/use-custom-container)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are applying transfer learning to train an image classifier from a pre-trained EfficientNet model. Your training dataset contains 20,000 images, and you intend to retrain the model once each day. You must minimize infrastructure costs. Which platform components and configuration environment should you use?

options.text: A Deep Learning VM with 4 V100 GPUs and local storage.
A Deep Learning VM with 4 V100 GPUs and Cloud Storage.
A Google Kubernetes Engine cluster with a V100 GPU Node Pool and an NFS Server
An AI Platform Training job using a custom scale tier with 4 V100 GPUs and Cloud Storage

questions.explanation:
A managed AI Platform Training job is appropriate for periodic batch training because compute resources are used for the submitted training run rather than maintained continuously. A custom scale tier can configure four NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPUs, while Cloud Storage provides persistent training data storage without operating VM-local storage or an NFS server.

**Learn more:** [gcloud ai-platform jobs submit training](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/ai-platform/jobs/submit/training)

questions.question: You are an ML engineer at a bank with a mobile application. Management has asked you to build ML-based biometric authentication for the app that verifies a customer’s identity from their fingerprint. Fingerprints are highly sensitive personal information and cannot be downloaded to or stored in the bank’s databases. Which learning strategy should you recommend to train and deploy this ML model?

options.text: Data Loss Prevention API
Federated learning
MD5 to encrypt data
Differential privacy

questions.explanation: Federated learning trains a common model using data that remains on customers’ devices or other local environments; only model updates are shared for aggregation. This supports biometric authentication without downloading or centrally storing raw fingerprint data in the bank’s databases.

questions.question: You are an ML engineer at a bank with a mobile application. Management has asked you to build ML-based biometric authentication for the app that verifies a customer’s identity from their fingerprint. Fingerprints are highly sensitive personal information and cannot be downloaded to or stored in the bank’s databases. Which learning strategy should you recommend to train and deploy this ML model?

options.text: Use the Apache Airflow SDK to create multiple operators that use Dataflow and Vertex AI services. Deploy the workflow on Cloud Composer.
Use the MLFlow SDK and deploy it on a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster. Create multiple components that use Dataflow and Vertex AI services.
Use the Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) SDK to create multiple components that use Dataflow and Vertex AI services. Deploy the workflow on Vertex AI Pipelines.
Use the TensorFlow Extended (TFX) SDK to create multiple components that use Dataflow and Vertex AI services. Deploy the workflow on Vertex AI Pipelines.

This combination directly supports the required end-to-end TensorFlow workflow with minimal infrastructure management.

Your team regularly develops new ML models and conducts experiments. The team pushes code to a single repository hosted in Cloud Source Repositories. You want to create a continuous integration pipeline that automatically retrains the models whenever any code is modified. What should be your first step in setting up the CI pipeline?

options.text: Configure a Cloud Build trigger with the event set as
Configure a Cloud Build trigger with the event set as
Configure a Cloud Function that builds the repository each time there is a code change
Configure a Cloud Function that builds the repository each time a new branch is created

questions.explanation:
A Cloud Build trigger configured for **Push to a branch** automatically starts a build whenever commits are pushed to the selected repository branch. That build can run the model-retraining workflow, satisfying continuous integration for code changes.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for an organization that runs a streaming music service. A custom production model serves a “next song” recommendation based on a user's recent listening history. The model is deployed to a Vertex AI endpoint. You recently retrained the same model using fresh data, and it produced positive offline test results. You now want to test the new model in production while minimizing complexity. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new Vertex AI endpoint for the new model and deploy the new model to that new endpoint. Build a service to randomly send 5% of production traffic to the new endpoint. Monitor end-user metrics such as listening time. If end-user metrics improve between models over time, gradually increase the percentage of production traffic sent to the new endpoint.

Capture incoming prediction requests in BigQuery. Create an experiment in Vertex AI Experiments. Run batch predictions for both models using the captured data. Use the user’s selected song to compare the models performance side by side. If the new model’s performance metrics are better than the previous model, deploy the new model to production.

If end-user metrics improve between models over time, gradually increase the percentage of production traffic sent to the new model.

Configure a model monitoring job for the existing Vertex AI endpoint. Configure the monitoring job to detect prediction drift and set a threshold for alerts. questions.explanation:
A Vertex AI public endpoint can host multiple deployed models and split its incoming prediction traffic among them by percentage. Deploying the retrained model to the existing endpoint and initially routing 5% of traffic to it provides a controlled production comparison using real end-user metrics, such as listening time; the traffic share can be increased as the new model demonstrates better outcomes.

**Learn more:** [Vertex AI API reference: Endpoint traffic_split](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1)

Your organization runs an online message board. A few months ago, you noticed an increase in toxic language and bullying on the board. You deployed an automated text classifier that flags some comments as toxic or harmful. Now, some users report that benign comments referring to their religion are being incorrectly classified as abusive. After further inspection, you determine that the classifier’s false-positive rate is higher for comments that refer to certain underrepresented religious groups. Your team is already overextended and has a limited budget. What should you do?

options.text: Add synthetic training data where those phrases are used in non-toxic ways.
Remove the model and replace it with human moderation.
Replace your model with a different text classifier.
Raise the threshold for comments to be considered toxic or harmful.

questions.explanation:
A higher false-positive rate for underrepresented religious groups indicates biased or insufficiently representative training data. Adding carefully validated synthetic benign examples containing the affected phrases augments the minority subgroup’s data, helping the classifier learn that those references are not inherently toxic while retaining automated moderation. Google’s fairness guidance identifies augmenting training data as a primary bias-mitigation strategy and recommends increasing representation for underrepresented groups.

**Learn more:** [Fairness: Mitigating bias | Google for Developers](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/fairness/mitigating-bias) · [AI and ML ethics and safety | Google for Developers](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/managing-ml-projects/ethics)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work at a large retailer and need to build a model to predict customer chum. The company has a dataset of historical customer data, including customer demographics, purchase history, and website activity. You need to create the model in BigQuery ML and thoroughly assess its performance. What should you do?

options.text: Create a linear regression model in BigQuery ML, and register the model in Vertex AI Model Registry. Evaluate the model performance in Vertex AI .
Create a logistic regression model in BigQuery ML and register the model in Vertex AI Model Registry. Evaluate the model performance in Vertex AI .
Create a linear regression model in BigQuery ML. Use the ML.EVALUATE function to evaluate the model performance.
Create a logistic regression model in BigQuery ML. Use the ML.CONFUSION_MATRIX function to evaluate the model performance.

questions.explanation:
Customer churn is a classification target, so a BigQuery ML logistic regression model is appropriate. `ML.CONFUSION_MATRIX` evaluates a classification model by reporting predicted classes against expected labels, allowing errors such as false positives and false negatives to be assessed. Google Cloud documents logistic regression as a classification model and supports `ML.CONFUSION_MATRIX` for its evaluation.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery ML model evaluation overview](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/evaluate-overview) · [The ML.CONFUSION_MATRIX function](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-confusion)

You work for a food-product company. The company’s historical sales data is stored in BigQuery. You need to use Vertex AI’s custom training service to train multiple TensorFlow models that read data from BigQuery and predict future sales.  
  
You plan to implement a data-preprocessing algorithm that performs mm-max scaling and bucketing on a large number of features before beginning model experimentation. You want to minimize preprocessing time, cost, and development effort. How should you configure this workflow?

options.text: Write the transformations into Spark that uses the spark-bigquery-connector, and use Dataproc to preprocess the data.
Write SQL queries to transform the data in-place in BigQuery.
Add the transformations as a preprocessing layer in the TensorFlow models.
Create a Dataflow pipeline that uses the BigQuerylO connector to ingest the data, process it, and write it back to BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery SQL can transform data where it is stored, avoiding a separate Spark/Dataproc or Dataflow processing environment and unnecessary data movement. Materializing the transformed data in BigQuery makes the shared scaling and bucketing results available to multiple TensorFlow training experiments without duplicating preprocessing logic in every model.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a company developing an application to help users plan meals. You want to use machine learning to scan a corpus of recipes and extract every ingredient (for example, carrot, rice, pasta) and each item of kitchen cookware (for example, bowl, pot, spoon) mentioned. Each recipe is stored in an unstructured text file. What should you do?

options.text: Create a text dataset on Vertex AI for entity extraction Create two entities called “ingredient” and “cookware”, and label at least 200 examples of each entity. Train an AutoML entity extraction model to extract occurrences of these entity types. Evaluate performance on a holdout dataset.

Create a multi-label text classification dataset on Vertex AI. Create a test dataset, and label each recipe that corresponds to its ingredients and cookware. Train a multi-class classification model. Evaluate the model’s performance on a holdout dataset.
Use the Entity Analysis method of the Natural Language API to extract the ingredients and cookware from each recipe. Evaluate the model's performance on a prelabeled dataset.

Create a text dataset on Vertex AI for entity extraction. Create as many entities as there are different ingredients and cookware. Train an AutoML entity extraction model to extract those entities. Evaluate the model’s performance on a holdout dataset.

questions.explanation:
Custom entity extraction identifies annotated text spans and assigns each span a label. Labeling recipe mentions with the two entity types `ingredient` and `cookware`, training an entity-extraction model, and evaluating it on held-out data lets the model recognize many individual ingredients and cookware items without treating every possible item as a separate class. Text classification labels an entire recipe rather than the mentions within it, while generic Entity Analysis does not supply these custom domain-specific categories.

**Learn more:** [Use managed datasets — Vertex AI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/training/using-managed-datasets)

questions.explanation:

questions.question: You are building an ML model with a dataset containing categorical input variables. You randomly split the data equally into training and test sets. After one-hot encoding the categorical variables in the training set, you find that one categorical variable is absent from the test set. What should you do?

options.text: Use sparse representation in the test set.
Randomly redistribute the data, with 70% for the training set and 30% for the test set
Apply one-hot encoding on the categorical variables in the test data
Collect more data representing all categories

questions.explanation: One-hot encoding requires consistent category-derived features across training and evaluation data. Data representing every category is needed so that each category can be included and evaluated rather than being absent from the test split.

options.text: Use Vertex Explainable AI for model explainability. Configure feature-based explanations.
Use Vertex Explainable AI for model explainability. Configure example-based explanations.
Create a Vertex AI Model Monitoring job. Enable training-serving skew detection for your model.
Create a Vertex AI Model Monitoring job. Enable feature attribution skew and drift detection for your model.

questions.explanation:
Feature-attribution monitoring tracks changes over time in each input feature’s contribution to predictions, which can indicate model-performance degradation caused by distribution drift. Training-serving skew detection requires the original training data as its baseline, whereas attribution drift monitoring can be used when that training data is not available in the cloud.

**Learn more:** [Monitor feature attribution skew and drift](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/model-monitoring/monitor-explainable-ai?hl=en) · [Best practices for implementing machine learning on Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/ml-on-gcp-best-practices)

questions.question: You are an ML engineer at a global shoe retailer and manage the ML models for the company’s website. You have been asked to build a model that recommends new products to users based on their purchase behavior and similarities to other users. What should you do?

options.text: Build a classification model
Build a knowledge-based filtering model
Build a collaborative-based filtering model
Build a regression model using the features as predictors

questions.explanation: Collaborative filtering recommends products by using patterns in user behavior—such as purchases—and similarities between users to infer products a user is likely to prefer.

options.text: Use Vertex Explainable AI with the sampled Shapley method, and enable Vertex AI Model Monitoring to check for feature distribution drift.
Use Vertex Explainable AI with the sampled Shapley method, and enable Vertex AI Model Monitoring to check for feature distribution skew.
Use Vertex Explainable AI with the XRAI method, and enable Vertex AI Model Monitoring to check for feature distribution drift.
Use Vertex Explainable AI with the XRAI method, and enable Vertex AI Model Monitoring to check for feature distribution skew.

questions.explanation:
Sampled Shapley provides feature-attribution explanations suited to tabular classification and regression, including neural-network models. XRAI redistributes attributions across segmented image regions, so it is not the appropriate method for a feature-based credit-risk model. Feature-distribution drift detection identifies significant changes in production input data over time; skew detection instead identifies differences between training and serving distributions.

**Learn more:** [Vertex Explainable AI overview](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/explainable-ai/overview) · [Introduction to Vertex AI Model Monitoring](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/model-monitoring/overview)

You created a custom Vertex AI pipeline job that preprocesses images and trains an object-detection model. The pipeline currently uses one `n1-standard-8` machine with one NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU. You want to shorten model-training time without reducing model accuracy. What should you do?

options.text: Reduce the number of layers in your object detection model.

Update the WorkerPoolSpec to use a machine with 24 vCPUs and 1 NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU.
Update the WorkerPoolSpec to use a machine with 24 vCPUs and 3 NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPUs.

questions.explanation:
Training the same model on the complete dataset preserves the model architecture and training data, while additional CPU and GPU resources can reduce wall-clock training time when the training code supports multi-GPU execution. You are responsible for managing and monitoring a Vertex AI model deployed in production. You want the model to be retrained automatically when its performance degrades. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Vertex AI Model Monitoring job to track the model's performance with production data, and trigger retraining when specific metrics drop below predefined thresholds.
Collect feedback from end users, and retrain the model based on their assessment of its performance.
Configure a scheduled job to evaluate the model's performance on a static dataset, and retrain the model if the performance drops below predefined thresholds.
Use Vertex Explainable AI to analyze feature attributions and identify potential biases in the model. Retrain when significant shifts in feature importance or biases are detected.

questions.explanation:

You are implementing a batch-inference ML pipeline in Google Cloud. The model was developed with TensorFlow and is stored in SavedModel format in Cloud Storage. options.text: Export the historical data to Cloud Storage in Avro format. Configure a Vertex AI batch prediction job to generate predictions for the exported data
Import the TensorFlow model by using the CREATE MODEL statement in BigQuery ML. Apply the historical data to the TensorFlow model
Export the historical data to Cloud Storage in CSV format. Configure a Vertex AI batch prediction job to generate predictions for the exported data
Configure a Vertex AI batch prediction job to apply the model to the historical data in BigQuery

questions.explanation:
BigQuery ML can import a TensorFlow model in SavedModel format from Cloud Storage by using `CREATE MODEL` with `MODEL_TYPE='TENSORFLOW'` and `MODEL_PATH`. The imported model can then generate predictions directly over BigQuery data with `ML.PREDICT`, which is appropriate for a 10 TB table and avoids exporting the data to Cloud Storage.

**Learn more:** [CREATE MODEL statement for importing TensorFlow models](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-create-tensorflow) · [Make predictions with imported TensorFlow models](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/making-predictions-with-imported-tensorflow-models)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a company that operates a ticketing platform for a large cinema chain. Customers use a mobile app to find movies that interest them and buy tickets through the app. Ticket-purchase requests are sent to Pub/Sub and processed by a Dataflow streaming pipeline configured to perform these steps:  
  
1. Verify the availability of movie tickets at the chosen cinema.  
2. Set the ticket price and accept payment.  
3. Reserve the tickets at the chosen cinema.  
4. Send successful purchases to your database.  
  
Every step in this process has low-latency requirements (under 50 milliseconds). You developed a logistic-regression model with BigQuery ML that predicts whether offering a free-popcorn promo code increases the likelihood of a ticket purchase, and this prediction must be added to the ticket-purchase process. You want to determine the simplest way to deploy this model to production while adding minimal latency. What should you do?

options.text: Run batch inference with BigQuery ML every five minutes on each new set of tickets issued.
Export your model in TensorFlow format, and add a tfx_bsl.public.beam.RunInference step to the Dataflow pipeline.
Export your model in TensorFlow format, deploy it on Vertex AI, and query the prediction endpoint from your streaming pipeline.
Convert your model with TensorFlow Lite (TFLite), and add it to the mobile app so that the promo code and the incoming request arrive together in Pub/Sub.

questions.explanation:
A BigQuery ML `LOGISTIC_REG` model can be exported as a TensorFlow SavedModel. TFX-BSL's `RunInference` uses a TensorFlow model handler to run predictions inside an Apache Beam pipeline, so the streaming Dataflow workers can perform inference locally rather than making a remote prediction-endpoint call. This provides the simplest integration with minimal added latency for the purchase flow.

**Learn more:** [Export models | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/exporting-models) · [Use RunInference with TFX Basic Shared Libraries | Dataflow ML | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/notebooks/run_inference_tensorflow_with_tfx)

options.text: Use the interleave option for reading data.
Reduce the value of the repeat parameter.
Increase the buffer size for the shuttle option.
Set the prefetch option equal to the training batch size.
Decrease the batch size argument in your transformation.

questions.explanation:
An input-bound TPU means the tf.data pipeline cannot feed the accelerator fast enough, so the fixes must parallelize I/O and overlap data preparation with computation. Using interleave for reading (A) parallelizes reading and decoding across multiple files, and setting prefetch (D) overlaps input preprocessing with model execution so the TPU is not left idle waiting for the next batch. Increasing the shuffle buffer (C) improves randomness and consumes more memory but does not relieve the input bottleneck, reducing the repeat value (B) only changes how many epochs are produced, and decreasing the batch size (E) reduces throughput and can leave the TPU underutilized. Therefore interleave and prefetch (A and D) are the two changes that address the bottleneck.

**Learn more:** [Better performance with the tf.data API](https://www.tensorflow.org/guide/data_performance) · [Analyze tf.data performance with the TF Profiler](https://www.tensorflow.org/guide/data_performance_analysis)

You are the Director of Data Science at a large company, and your Data Science team has recently started using the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK to orchestrate its training pipelines. The team is finding it difficult to integrate custom Python code into the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK. How should you direct them to proceed to integrate their code with the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK quickly?

options.text: Use the func_to_container_op function to create custom components from the Python code.
Use the predefined components available in the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK to access Dataproc, and run the custom code there.
Package the custom Python code into Docker containers, and use the load_component_from_file function to import the containers into the pipeline.
Deploy the custom Python code to Cloud Functions, and use Kubeflow Pipelines to trigger the Cloud Function.

questions.explanation:
In Kubeflow Pipelines SDK v1, `kfp.components.func_to_container_op` converts a standalone Python function into a pipeline component factory, allowing the custom code to run as a containerized pipeline task with minimal integration work. Current SDK v2 uses the `@dsl.component` decorator instead, but `func_to_container_op` is the applicable legacy SDK mechanism.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to the Pipelines SDK (legacy v1)](https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/components/pipelines/legacy-v1/sdk/sdk-overview/) · [Migrate to Kubeflow Pipelines v2](https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/components/pipelines/user-guides/migration/)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company’s business stakeholders need to understand the factors that drive customer churn to guide their business strategy. You must build a customer-churn prediction model that emphasizes simple interpretation of the model results. You need to select the ML framework and modeling technique that explains which features led to the prediction. What should you do?

options.text: Build a TensorFlow deep neural network (DNN) model, and use SHAP values for feature importance analysis.
Build a PyTorch long short-term memory (LSTM) network, and use attention mechanisms for interpretability.
Build a logistic regression model in scikit-learn, and interpret the model's output coefficients to understand feature impact.
Build a linear regression model in scikit-learn, and interpret the model's standardized coefficients to understand feature impact.

questions.explanation:
Customer churn is a classification outcome, and logistic regression is a linear classifier with directly inspectable feature coefficients. Each coefficient expresses a feature’s direction and relative effect on the model’s churn log-odds, making the model suitable when simple, built-in interpretability is the priority. scikit-learn documents `LogisticRegression` as a classification model and exposes feature coefficients through `coef_`.

**Learn more:** [scikit-learn LogisticRegression API reference](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression.html) · [scikit-learn Linear Models: Logistic regression](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/linear_model.html)

You created the instance and ran the code, but the job now fails with an insufficient-permissions error. What should you do?

options.text: Ensure that the Workbench instance that you created is in the same region of the Vertex AI Pipelines resources you will use.
Ensure that the Vertex AI Workbench instance is on the same subnetwork of the Vertex AI Pipeline resources that you will use.
Ensure that the Vertex AI Workbench instance is assigned the Identity and Access Management (IAM) Vertex AI User role.
Ensure that the Vertex AI Workbench instance is assigned the Identity and Access Management (IAM) Notebooks Runner role.

questions.explanation:
Code running from a Vertex AI Workbench instance uses the identity of its attached service account, so that identity requires permissions to use Vertex AI and submit pipeline jobs. The Vertex AI User role (`roles/aiplatform.user`) provides the relevant Vertex AI permissions; matching a region or subnetwork does not resolve IAM authorization.

**Learn more:** [Use Private Service Connect to access training pipelines from on-premises](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/vertex-psc-pipelines)

You plan to deploy the model for an internal use case. You need full control over the model's underlying infrastructure and want to minimize the model's inference time. Which serving configuration should you use for this task?

options.text: Deploy the model on a Vertex AI endpoint manually by creating a custom inference container.
Deploy the model on a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster by using the deployment options in Model Garden.
Deploy the model on a Vertex AI endpoint by using one-click deployment in Model Garden.
Deploy the model on a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster manually by cresting a custom yaml manifest.

questions.explanation:
GKE provides granular control over infrastructure and complex AI/ML workload resource management. Deploying Gemma to GKE through Model Garden combines that infrastructure control with Google-provided deployment options for optimized model serving, supporting low-latency inference without requiring a fully manual Kubernetes manifest.

",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Use the aiplatform.log_classification_metrics function to log the F1 score, and use the aiplatform.log_metrics function to log the confusion matrix.","B":"Use the aiplatform.log_classification_metrics function to log the F1 score and the confusion matrix.","C":"Use the aiplatform.log_metrics function to log the F1 score and the confusion matrix.","D":"Use the aiplatform.log_metrics function to log the F1 score: and use the aiplatform.log_classification_metrics function to log the confusion matrix."},"correctAnswer":"D","explanation":"`aiplatform.log_metrics` logs scalar key/value metrics such as an F1 score. `aiplatform.log_classification_metrics` creates and logs a classification-metrics artifact that supports a confusion matrix, including its labels and matrix values.

52:[["$","p",null,{"children":"You are the Director of Data Science at a large company, and your Data Science team has recently started using the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK to orchestrate its training pipelines. The team is finding it difficult to integrate custom Python code into the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK. How should you direct them to proceed to integrate their code with the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK quickly?"}],"
",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Use the func_to_container_op function to create custom components from the Python code.","B":"Use the predefined components available in the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK to access Dataproc, and run the custom code there.","C":"Package the custom Python code into Docker containers, and use the load_component_from_file function to import the containers into the pipeline.","D":"Deploy the custom Python code to Cloud Functions, and use Kubeflow Pipelines to trigger the Cloud Function."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"In Kubeflow Pipelines SDK v1, `kfp.components.func_to_container_op` converts a standalone Python function into a pipeline component factory, allowing the custom code to run as a containerized pipeline task with minimal integration work. Current SDK v2 uses the `@dsl.component` decorator instead, but `func_to_container_op` is the applicable legacy SDK mechanism.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to the Pipelines SDK (legacy v1)](https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/components/pipelines/legacy-v1/sdk/sdk-overview/) · [Migrate to Kubeflow Pipelines v2](https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/components/pipelines/user-guides/migration/)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"5e04d029-1225-4d0b-a413-03e639f7bb8f","examProvider":"google","examName":"professional-machine-learning-engineer","mode":"default"}}]]
53:[["$","p",null,{"children":"Your company’s business stakeholders need to understand the factors that drive customer churn to guide their business strategy. You must build a customer-churn prediction model that emphasizes simple interpretation of the model results. You need to select the ML framework and modeling technique that explains which features led to the prediction. What should you do?"}],"
",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Build a TensorFlow deep neural network (DNN) model, and use SHAP values for feature importance analysis.","B":"Build a PyTorch long short-term memory (LSTM) network, and use attention mechanisms for interpretability.","C":"Build a logistic regression model in scikit-learn, and interpret the model's output coefficients to understand feature impact.","D":"Build a linear regression model in scikit-learn, and interpret the model's standardized coefficients to understand feature impact."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"Customer churn is a classification outcome, and logistic regression is a linear classifier with directly inspectable feature coefficients. Each coefficient expresses a feature’s direction and relative effect on the model’s churn log-odds, making the model suitable when simple, built-in interpretability is the priority. scikit-learn documents `LogisticRegression` as a classification model and exposes feature coefficients through `coef_`.

**Learn more:** [scikit-learn LogisticRegression API reference](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression.html) · [scikit-learn Linear Models: Logistic regression](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/linear_model.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"c36f87af-6cf9-44f3-9b9a-6c9e5babf576","examProvider":"google","examName":"professional-machine-learning-engineer","mode":"default"}}]]
54:[["$","p",null,{"children":"You recently created a new Google Cloud project. ",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Ensure that the Workbench instance that you created is in the same region of the Vertex AI Pipelines resources you will use.","B":"Ensure that the Vertex AI Workbench instance is on the same subnetwork of the Vertex AI Pipeline resources that you will use.","C":"Ensure that the Vertex AI Workbench instance is assigned the Identity and Access Management (IAM) Vertex AI User role.","D":"Ensure that the Vertex AI Workbench instance is assigned the Identity and Access Management (IAM) Notebooks Runner role."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"Code running from a Vertex AI Workbench instance uses the identity of its attached service account, so that identity requires permissions to use Vertex AI and submit pipeline jobs. The Vertex AI User role (`roles/aiplatform.user`) provides the relevant Vertex AI permissions; matching a region or subnetwork does not resolve IAM authorization.

**Learn more:** [Use Private Service Connect to access training pipelines from on-premises](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/vertex-psc-pipelines)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"e40edbbf-7a0f-42f6-a80a-65d13c78027b","examProvider":"google","examName":"professional-machine-learning-engineer","mode":"default"}}]]
55:[["$","p",null,{"children":"You are an ML researcher at an investment bank and are experimenting with the Gemma large language model (LLM). You plan to deploy the model for an internal use case. ",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Deploy the model on a Vertex AI endpoint manually by creating a custom inference container.","B":"Deploy the model on a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster by using the deployment options in Model Garden.","C":"Deploy the model on a Vertex AI endpoint by using one-click deployment in Model Garden.","D":"Deploy the model on a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster manually by cresting a custom yaml manifest."},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"GKE provides granular control over infrastructure and complex AI/ML workload resource management. **Learn more:** [Use Gemma open models](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/open-models/use-gemma) · [What is inference optimization?](https://cloud.google.com/discover/inference-optimization)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"9550c4f4-1211-43c1-81ac-cf303de98ffe","examProvider":"google","examName":"professional-machine-learning-engineer","mode":"default"}}]]
You are on a data science team at a bank, developing an ML model to predict loan-default risk. You have gathered and cleaned hundreds of millions of training-data records in a BigQuery table, and now want to develop and compare multiple models using TensorFlow and Vertex AI. You want to minimize bottlenecks during the data-ingestion stage while accounting for scalability. What should you do?

options.text: Use the BigQuery client library to load data into a dataframe, and use tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices() to read it.
Export data to CSV files in Cloud Storage, and use tf.data.TextLineDataset() to read them.
Convert the data into TFRecords, and use tf.data.TFRecordDataset() to read them.
Use TensorFlow I/O’s BigQuery Reader to directly read the data.

questions.explanation:
TensorFlow I/O’s BigQuery reader can create a BigQuery read session and read the table through multiple parallel streams, providing a scalable `tf.data.Dataset` directly from BigQuery. This avoids materializing hundreds of millions of records in a client-side dataframe and avoids the additional export and file-conversion pipeline required for CSV or TFRecord files.

**Learn more:** [tfio.bigquery.BigQueryReadSession](https://www.tensorflow.org/io/api_docs/python/tfio/bigquery/BigQueryReadSession) · [Reading and storing data for custom model training on Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/reading-and-storing-data-custom-model-training-vertex-ai)
