You work for a hospital. You received approval to collect the required patient data and trained a Vertex AI tabular AutoML model that calculates patients’ risk scores for hospital admission. You deployed the model. However, you are concerned that patient demographics could change over time, changing feature interactions and affecting prediction accuracy. You want to receive alerts when feature interactions change, and you want to understand the features’ importance to predictions. You want your alerting approach to minimize cost. What should you do?

options.text: Create a feature drift monitoring job. Set the sampling rate to 1 and the monitoring frequency to weekly.
Create a feature drift monitoring job. Set the sampling rate to 0.1 and the monitoring frequency to weekly.
Create a feature attribution drift monitoring job. Set the sampling rate to 1 and the monitoring frequency to weekly.
Create a feature attribution drift monitoring job. Set the sampling rate to 0.1 and the monitoring frequency to weekly.

questions.explanation:
Feature attribution drift monitoring tracks changes in each feature’s contribution to model predictions, providing feature-importance information. Feature attributions account for both individual feature effects and interactions with other features, so shifts in those interactions can be detected even when a feature’s marginal distribution is unchanged. Using a 0.1 sampling rate processes fewer incoming prediction requests than full sampling and therefore minimizes monitoring cost.

**Learn more:** [Monitor feature attribution skew and drift](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/model-monitoring/monitor-explainable-ai)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for an auto-insurance company and are preparing a proof-of-concept ML application that uses images of damaged vehicles to identify damaged parts. Your team has assembled annotated images from damage-claim documents in the company database. The annotations for each image include a bounding box for every identified damaged part and the part name. You have a sufficient budget to train models on Google Cloud. You need to create an initial model quickly. What should you do?

options.text: Download a pre-trained object detection model from TensorFlow Hub. Fine-tune the model in Vertex AI Workbench by using the annotated image data.
Train an object detection model in AutoML by using the annotated image data.
Create a pipeline in Vertex AI Pipelines and configure the AutoMLTrainingJobRunOp component to train a custom object detection model by using the annotated image data.
Train an object detection model in Vertex AI custom training by using the annotated image data.

questions.explanation:
Image annotations consisting of labeled bounding boxes are training data for object detection. Vertex AI AutoML can train an image object-detection model directly from such an annotated dataset with minimal custom code, making it the fastest suitable approach for an initial proof of concept.

**Learn more:** [Train an image object detection model](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/image-data/object-detection/train-model) · [Create a training pipeline for image object detection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/samples/aiplatform-create-training-pipeline-image-object-detection-sample)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to build an image-classification model using a large dataset of labeled images stored in a Cloud Storage bucket. What should you do?

options.text: Use Vertex AI Pipelines with the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK to create a pipeline that reads the images from Cloud Storage and trains the model.
Use Vertex AI Pipelines with TensorFlow Extended (TFX) to create a pipeline that reads the images from Cloud Storage and trains the model.
Import the labeled images as a managed dataset in Vertex AI and use AutoML to train the model.
Convert the image dataset to a tabular format using Dataflow Load the data into BigQuery and use BigQuery ML to train the model.

questions.explanation:
Vertex AI supports importing labeled images from Cloud Storage into a managed image dataset and training an AutoML image-classification model from that dataset. This is the managed service path designed for labeled image-classification data.

**Learn more:** [Train an image classification model | Vertex AI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/image-data/classification/train-model) · [Use managed datasets | Vertex AI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/training/using-managed-datasets)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are training a deep learning model for semantic image segmentation while reducing training time. When using a Deep Learning VM Image, you receive this error: `The resource 'projects/deeplearning-platforn/zones/europe-west4-c/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-k80' was not found.` What should you do?

options.text: Ensure that you have GPU quota in the selected region.
Ensure that the required GPU is available in the selected region.
Ensure that you have preemptible GPU quota in the selected region.
Ensure that the selected GPU has enough GPU memory for the workload.

questions.explanation:
Compute Engine accelerator types are zone-specific: a VM can use a GPU only in a zone where that accelerator type is available. A not-found accelerator resource indicates that the requested GPU is unavailable in the selected location, rather than that the project lacks quota. NVIDIA Tesla K80 GPUs are also no longer supported on Google Cloud.

**Learn more:** [GPU locations](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/regions-zones/gpu-regions-zones) · [NVIDIA K80 end of support](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/eol/k80-eol)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a retail company and have been assigned to build a model that determines each customer's probability of churn. The predictions must be interpretable so the results can be used to develop marketing campaigns targeting at-risk customers. What should you do?

options.text: Build a random forest regression model in a Vertex AI Workbench notebook instance. Configure the model to generate feature importances after the model is trained.
Build an AutoML tabular regression model. Configure the model to generate explanations when it makes predictions.
Build a custom TensorFlow neural network by using Vertex AI custom training. Configure the model to generate explanations when it makes predictions.
Build a random forest classification model in a Vertex AI Workbench notebook instance. Configure the model to generate feature importances after the model is trained.

questions.explanation:
Churn is a binary classification outcome, and an at-risk marketing campaign needs per-customer feature attributions that explain an individual churn-probability prediction. A custom TensorFlow model can be configured with Vertex Explainable AI to return those prediction explanations. Global random-forest feature importances describe overall model behavior, not the reasons for a specific customer's prediction.

**Learn more:** [Use TensorFlow for explanations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/explainable-ai/tensorflow) · [Introduction to tabular data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/tabular-data/tabular101)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team trained and tested a DNN regression model with good outcomes. Six months after deployment, it is performing poorly because the input-data distribution has changed. How should you address the input differences in production?

options.text: Create alerts to monitor for skew, and retrain the model.
Perform feature selection on the model, and retrain the model with fewer features.
Retrain the model, and select an L2 regularization parameter with a hyperparameter tuning service.
Perform feature selection on the model, and retrain the model on a monthly basis with fewer features.

questions.explanation:
A change between training and production input-feature distributions is training-serving skew (data drift), which can reduce production model quality. Monitor the input distributions for skew, alert when thresholds are exceeded, and retrain the model using data representative of the current production distribution.

**Learn more:** [Monitor models for training-serving skew with Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/monitor-models-training-serving-skew-vertex-ai) · [Introduction to Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/ai-platform/docs?o=7639)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have deployed several versions of an image-classification model on AI Platform. You want to track the performance of the model versions over time. How should you make this comparison?

options.text: Compare the loss performance for each model on a held-out dataset.
Compare the loss performance for each model on the validation data.
Compare the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve for each model using the What-If Tool.
Compare the mean average precision across the models using the Continuous Evaluation feature.

questions.explanation:
AI Platform Continuous Evaluation repeatedly evaluates sampled online predictions from deployed model versions over time, allowing their performance metrics to be compared as production data changes. Mean average precision provides an aggregate quality measure for image-classification predictions.

**Learn more:** [Model evaluation in Agent Platform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/evaluation/introduction)

questions.question: While training a neural network in batches, you observe oscillation in the loss. How should you modify the model to ensure convergence?

options.text: Decrease the size of the training batch.
Decrease the learning rate hyperparameter.
Increase the learning rate hyperparameter.
Increase the size of the training batch.

questions.explanation:
A learning rate that is too high can make gradient-based updates overshoot the loss minimum repeatedly, producing oscillation. Lowering the learning-rate hyperparameter reduces each update’s step size and enables more stable convergence.\
\
**Learn more:** [TensorFlow: Training and evaluation with built-in methods](https://www.tensorflow.org/guide/keras/training_with_built_in_methods) · [TensorFlow: ExponentialDecay learning-rate schedule](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/keras/optimizers/schedules/ExponentialDecay)

questions.question: While training a neural network in batches, you observe oscillation in the loss. How should you modify the model to ensure convergence?

options.text: Apply tf.data.Detaset.map with vectorized operations and parallelization.
Use tf.data.Detaset.interleave with multiple data sources.
Use tf.data.Detaset.cache on the dataset after the first epoch.
Implement tf.data.Detaset.prefetch in the data pipeline.

questions.explanation:
`tf.data.Dataset.prefetch` decouples data production from data consumption by buffering upcoming batches and overlapping input-pipeline preprocessing with the current training step. This prevents the TPU from waiting for the next batch and improves utilization when gaps occur between steps.

**Learn more:** [Better performance with the tf.data API](https://www.tensorflow.org/guide/data_performance) · [Analyze tf.data performance with the TF Profiler](https://www.tensorflow.org/guide/data_performance_analysis)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a TensorFlow Extended (TFX) pipeline that uses standard TFX components. The pipeline contains data-preprocessing steps. After deployment to production, it will process up to 100 TB of data stored in BigQuery. You need the preprocessing steps to scale efficiently, publish metrics and parameters to Vertex AI Experiments, and track artifacts by using Vertex ML Metadata. How should you configure the pipeline run?

options.text: Run the TFX pipeline in Vertex AI Pipelines. Configure the pipeline to use Vertex AI Training jobs with distributed processing.
Run the TFX pipeline in Vertex AI Pipelines. Set the appropriate Apache Beam parameters in the pipeline to run the data preprocessing steps in Dataflow.
Run the TFX pipeline in Dataproc by using the Apache Beam TFX orchestrator. Set the appropriate Vertex AI permissions in the job to publish metadata in Vertex AI.
Run the TFX pipeline in Dataflow by using the Apache Beam TFX orchestrator. Set the appropriate Vertex AI permissions in the job to publish metadata in Vertex AI.

questions.explanation:
Standard TFX data-processing components use Apache Beam; TensorFlow Transform converts transformations to Beam processing. Configuring those components to use the Dataflow runner provides scalable distributed preprocessing for very large BigQuery datasets. Vertex AI Pipelines orchestrates TFX workflows and automatically records pipeline artifacts in Vertex ML Metadata, while pipeline runs can be compared using their parameters and metrics for experiment analysis.

**Learn more:** [Dataflow ML in ML workflows](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/machine-learning/ml-data) · [Architecture for MLOps using TensorFlow Extended, Vertex AI Pipelines, and Cloud Build](https://cloud.google.com/solutions/machine-learning/architecture-for-mlops-using-tfx-kubeflow-pipelines-and-cloud-build)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building an ML model to recognize your company’s products in images. You have access to more than one million images in a Cloud Storage bucket. You plan to test different TensorFlow models using Vertex AI Training. You need to read images at scale during training while minimizing data I/O bottlenecks. What should you do?

options.text: Load the images directly into the Vertex AI compute nodes by using Cloud Storage FUSE. Read the images by using the tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices function
Create a Vertex AI managed dataset from your image data. Access the AIP_TRAINING_DATA_URI environment variable to read the images by using the tf.data.Dataset.list_files function.
Convert the images to TFRecords and store them in a Cloud Storage bucket. Read the TFRecords by using the tf.data.TFRecordDataset function.
Store the URLs of the images in a CSV file. Read the file by using the tf.data.experimental.CsvDataset function.

questions.explanation:
TFRecord is TensorFlow’s record-oriented binary format for training data, and `tf.data.TFRecordDataset` streams one or more TFRecord files as an input pipeline. Converting many individual image objects into sharded TFRecord files reduces repeated object lookup and file-open overhead, enabling efficient sequential and parallel reads at training scale.

**Learn more:** [tf.data: Build TensorFlow input pipelines](https://www.tensorflow.org/guide/data) · [Analyze tf.data performance with the TF Profiler](https://www.tensorflow.org/guide/data_performance_analysis)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a large organization that has recently chosen to move its ML and data workloads to Google Cloud. The data engineering team exported structured data in Avro format to a Cloud Storage bucket. You need to propose a workflow that performs analytics, generates features, and serves the features used by ML models for online prediction. How should the pipeline be configured?

options.text: Ingest the Avro files into Cloud Spanner to perform analytics. Use a Dataflow pipeline to create the features, and store them in Vertex AI Feature Store for online prediction.
Ingest the Avro files into BigQuery to perform analytics. Use a Dataflow pipeline to create the features, and store them in Vertex AI Feature Store for online prediction.
Ingest the Avro files into Cloud Spanner to perform analytics. Use a Dataflow pipeline to create the features, and store them in BigQuery for online prediction.
Ingest the Avro files into BigQuery to perform analytics. Use BigQuery SQL to create features and store them in a separate BigQuery table for online prediction.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery is Google Cloud’s analytics data warehouse for structured data, Dataflow can perform scalable feature transformations, and Vertex AI Feature Store provides low-latency online serving of feature values for online predictions. Vertex AI Feature Store uses BigQuery feature data as its source while providing the online-serving capability.

**Learn more:** [Feature serving | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/feature-serving) · [Prepare data source | Vertex AI Feature Store | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/featurestore/latest/prepare-data-source)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You recently deployed an image-classification model on Google Cloud and used Cloud Build to create a CI/CD pipeline for the model. You need to ensure the model remains up to date with data and code changes through an efficient retraining process. What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud Run functions to monitor data drift in real time and trigger a Vertex AI Training job to retrain the model when data drift exceeds a predetermined threshold.
Configure a Git repository trigger in Cloud Build to initiate retraining when there are new code commits to the model's repository and a Pub/Sub trigger when there is new data in Cloud Storage.
Use Cloud Scheduler to initiate a daily retraining job in Vertex AI Pipelines.
Configure Cloud Composer to orchestrate a weekly retraining job that includes data extraction from BigQuery, model retraining with Vertex AI Training, and model deployment to a Vertex AI endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Build repository-event triggers can automatically run builds when new commits are pushed, and Cloud Build Pub/Sub triggers can run builds in response to messages generated for Cloud Storage events. This event-driven design retrains only when model code or input data changes, avoiding unnecessary fixed-interval retraining.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Build triggers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/triggers) · [Automate builds in response to Pub/Sub events](https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/automate-builds-pubsub-events)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are an ML engineer at an ecommerce company who has been assigned to build a model that predicts how much inventory the logistics team should order each month. Which approach should you use?

options.text: Use a clustering algorithm to group popular items together. Give the list to the logistics team so they can increase inventory of the popular items.

Use a regression model to predict how much additional inventory should be purchased each month. Give the results to the logistics team at the beginning of the month so they can increase inventory by the amount predicted by the model.
Use a time series forecasting model to predict each item's monthly sales. Give the results to the logistics team so they can base inventory on the amount predicted by the model.
Use a classification model to classify inventory levels as UNDER_STOCKED, OVER_STOCKED, and CORRECTLY_STOCKEGive the report to the logistics team each month so they can fine-tune inventory levels.

questions.explanation:
Time series forecasting predicts future values from historical time-indexed data. Forecasting each item's monthly sales captures demand trends and seasonality, giving the logistics team an appropriate basis for monthly inventory decisions.

**Learn more:** [Forecasting overview | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/forecasting-overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for an online travel agency that also sells advertising placements on its website to other companies. You have been asked to predict the most relevant web banner a user should see next. Security is important to your company. The model latency requirements are 300ms@p99, the inventory is thousands of web banners, and your exploratory analysis has shown that navigation context is a good predictor. You want to implement the simplest solution. How should you configure the prediction pipeline?

options.text: Embed the client on the website, and then deploy the model on AI Platform Prediction.
Embed the client on the website, deploy the gateway on App Engine, and then deploy the model on AI Platform Prediction.

Embed the client on the website, deploy the gateway on App Engine, deploy the database on Cloud Bigtable for writing and for reading the user's navigation context, and then deploy the model on AI Platform Prediction.

Embed the client on the website, deploy the gateway on App Engine, deploy the database on Memorystore for writing and for reading the user's navigation context, and then deploy the model on Google Kubernetes Engine.

questions.explanation:
A secure gateway on App Engine can mediate requests from the website, retrieve and update each user's navigation-context feature data in Cloud Bigtable, and call the managed AI Platform Prediction service. Bigtable is designed for scalable, low-latency key-value and wide-column workloads, including real-time personalization and high-throughput reads and writes, so it fits serving navigation context without introducing the operational overhead of running a model on GKE.

**Learn more:** [Bigtable: Fast, Flexible NoSQL](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable) · [Understand Bigtable performance](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/performance)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to rebuild an ML pipeline for structured data on Google Cloud. You use PySpark to perform transformations at scale, but the pipelines take more than 12 hours to complete. To accelerate development and pipeline execution, you want a serverless tool that uses SQL syntax. You have already moved the raw data to Cloud Storage. How should you build the pipeline on Google Cloud while satisfying the speed and processing requirements?

options.text: Use Data Fusion's GUI to build the transformation pipelines, and then write the data into BigQuery.
Convert your PySpark into SparkSQL queries to transform the data, and then run your pipeline on Dataproc to write the data into BigQuery.
Ingest your data into Cloud SQL, convert your PySpark commands into SQL queries to transform the data, and then use federated queries from BigQuery for machine learning.
Ingest your data into BigQuery using BigQuery Load, convert your PySpark commands into BigQuery SQL queries to transform the data, and then write the transformations to a new table.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery has a serverless architecture and a scalable distributed query engine. It can batch-load data from Cloud Storage, and BigQuery SQL can transform that data and write the results to a new table, eliminating the need to manage Spark infrastructure while supporting large-scale analytical processing.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery overview](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/introduction) · [Introduction to loading data](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a fraud-detection model with Keras and TensorFlow. Customer transaction records are held in a large BigQuery table. You must preprocess these records efficiently and cost-effectively before using them to train the model. The trained model will perform batch inference in BigQuery. How should you implement the preprocessing workflow?

options.text: Implement a preprocessing pipeline by using Apache Spark, and run the pipeline on Dataproc. Save the preprocessed data as CSV files in a Cloud Storage bucket.
Load the data into a pandas DataFrame. Implement the preprocessing steps using pandas transformations, and train the model directly on the DataFrame.
Perform preprocessing in BigQuery by using SQL. Use the BigQueryClient in TensorFlow to read the data directly from BigQuery.
Implement a preprocessing pipeline by using Apache Beam, and run the pipeline on Dataflow. Save the preprocessed data as CSV files in a Cloud Storage bucket.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery SQL preprocesses large transaction tables within the data warehouse, avoiding the cost and operational overhead of exporting data to CSV and running separate Spark or Beam infrastructure. Reading the prepared data directly from BigQuery into TensorFlow also supports an efficient training path, while keeping the data preparation aligned with BigQuery batch inference.

**Learn more:** [Feature preprocessing overview](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/preprocess-overview) · [Make predictions with imported TensorFlow models](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/making-predictions-with-imported-tensorflow-models)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have received a dataset containing sales predictions based on your company’s marketing activities. The data is structured, stored in BigQuery, and has been carefully maintained by a team of data analysts.  
  
You need to prepare a report that provides insights into the data’s predictive capabilities. You were asked to run several ML models with varying levels of sophistication, including simple models and multilayered neural networks. You have only a few hours to collect the results of your experiments.  
  
Which Google Cloud tools should you use to complete this task in the most efficient and self-service manner?

options.text: Use BigQuery ML to run several regression models, and analyze their performance.
Read the data from BigQuery using Dataproc, and run several models using SparkML.
Use Vertex AI Workbench user-managed notebooks with scikit-learn code for a variety of ML algorithms and performance metrics.
Train a custom TensorFlow model with Vertex AI, reading the data from BigQuery featuring a variety of ML algorithms.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery ML enables self-service creation, training, prediction, and evaluation of machine learning models directly on structured data in BigQuery using SQL. It supports both linear regression and deep neural network regression models, allowing rapid comparison of simple and multilayer models without moving data or provisioning and coding a separate Spark, notebook, or custom TensorFlow training environment.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery ML regression overview](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/regression-overview) · [Create DNN models in BigQuery ML](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-create-dnn-models)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are an ML engineer at a bank. The bank’s leadership team wants to decrease the number of loan defaults. The bank stores labeled historical loan-default data in BigQuery. You have been asked to use AI to support the loan-application process. For compliance reasons, you must provide explanations for loan rejections. What should you do?

options.text: Import the historic loan default data into AutoML. Train and deploy a linear regression model to predict default probability. Report the probability of default for each loan application.

Create a custom application that uses the Gemini large language model (LLM). Provide the historic data as context to the model, and prompt the model to predict customer defaults. Report the prediction and explanation provided by the LLM for each loan application.

Train and deploy a BigQuery ML classification model trained on historic loan default data. Enable feature-based explanations for each prediction. Report the prediction, probability of default, and feature attributions for each loan application.

Load the historic loan default data into a Vertex AI Workbench instance. Train a deep learning classification model using TensorFlow to predict loan default. Run inference for each loan application, and report the predictions.

questions.explanation:
Loan default is a classification task because the historical labels indicate whether a default occurred. BigQuery ML can train classification models on BigQuery data and supports local Explainable AI feature attributions for each prediction. Reporting the predicted class, default probability, and per-application feature attributions provides the required decision explanation.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery Explainable AI overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/xai-overview) · [Classification overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/classification-overview)

options.text: Use the original audio sampling rate, and transcribe the audio by using the Speech-to-Text API with synchronous recognition.
Use the original audio sampling rate, and transcribe the audio by using the Speech-to-Text API with asynchronous recognition.
Downsample the audio recordings to 8 kHz, and transcribe the audio by using the Speech-to-Text API with synchronous recognition.
Downsample the audio recordings to 8 kHz, and transcribe the audio by using the Speech-to-Text API with asynchronous recognition.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Speech-to-Text uses asynchronous, long-running recognition for audio longer than 60 seconds; synchronous recognition is limited to one minute. Keeping the original 16 kHz sample rate preserves the supplied audio characteristics, and long-running recognition supports audio stored in Cloud Storage.

**Learn more:** [Transcribe long audio files into text](https://docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/v1/async-recognize) · [Cloud Speech-to-Text overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/overview)

You need to train an XGBoost model using a small dataset. Your training code needs custom dependencies, and you want to minimize your training job's startup time. How should you configure your Vertex AI custom training job?

options.text: Store the data in a Cloud Storage bucket, and create a custom container with your training application. In your training application, read the data from Cloud Storage and train the model.

Use the XGBoost prebuilt custom container. Create a Python source distribution that includes the data and installs the dependencies at runtime. In your training application, load the data into a pandas DataFrame and train the model.
Create a custom container that includes the data. In your training application, load the data into a pandas DataFrame and train the model.

Store the data in a Cloud Storage bucket, and use the XGBoost prebuilt custom container to run your training application. Create a Python source distribution that installs the dependencies at runtime. In your training application, read the data from Cloud Storage and train the model.

questions.explanation:
A custom training container can preinstall the training application and all custom dependencies, eliminating dependency-installation time when the job starts. Including a small dataset in that container also avoids fetching it from Cloud Storage at runtime, which minimizes startup overhead.

**Learn more:** [Vertex AI custom containers overview](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/training/containers-overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing a retraining policy for a customer-churn prediction model deployed in Vertex AI. New training data is added each week. You want to implement a model-retraining process that minimizes cost and effort. What should you do?

options.text: Retrain the model when a significant shift in the distribution of customer attributes is detected in the production data compared to the training data.
Retrain the model when the model's latency increases by 10% due to increased traffic.
Retrain the model when the model accuracy drops by 10% on the new training dataset.
Retrain the model every week when new training data is available.

questions.explanation:
A substantial change in the distribution of production customer attributes relative to the training-data baseline is training-serving skew or feature drift. Vertex AI Model Monitoring detects such shifts and alerts when incoming inference data differs sufficiently from the training baseline, making it an efficient event-driven signal for retraining. Retraining on a fixed weekly schedule can incur unnecessary training cost when the production data has not materially changed.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/ai-platform/docs) · [Provide schemas to Vertex AI Model Monitoring](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/model-monitoring/schemas)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are an ML engineer at a manufacturing company. You need to build a model that detects defects in products from images captured at the end of the assembly line. You want the model to preprocess the images with less computation so it can quickly extract defect features from products. Which approach should you use to build the model?

options.text: Reinforcement learning
Recommender system
Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN)
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)

questions.explanation:
Convolutional neural networks are suited to image-based defect detection because convolutional filters learn local spatial features, such as edges, textures, and irregularities, with shared weights. Pooling layers can downsample spatial data, reducing computation while preserving important features for classification or detection. questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You developed an AutoML tabular classification model that identifies high-value customers who interact with your organization's website. You plan to deploy the model to a new Vertex AI endpoint that integrates with your website application. You anticipate increased website traffic during nights and weekends. You need to configure the model endpoint deployment settings to minimize latency and cost. What should you do?

options.text: Configure the model deployment settings to use an n1-standard-32 machine type.
Configure the model deployment settings to use an n1-standard-4 machine type. Set the minReplicaCount value to 1 and the maxReplicaCount value to 8.
Configure the model deployment settings to use an n1-standard-4 machine type and a GPU accelerator. Set the minReplicaCount value to 1 and the maxReplicaCount value to 4.
Configure the model deployment settings to use an n1-standard-8 machine type and a GPU accelerator.

questions.explanation:
AutoML tabular models should use CPU serving rather than GPUs, because accelerators are not recommended for AutoML models. Setting `minReplicaCount` to 1 minimizes the always-on serving cost, and setting `maxReplicaCount` to 8 permits automatic scaling to accommodate higher inference demand, helping maintain low latency during traffic peaks.

**Learn more:** [Get online inferences for AutoML models](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/tabular-data/classification-regression/get-online-predictions) · [AutomaticResources](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1beta1/AutomaticResources)

You manage a data science team working on a computationally intensive project that requires running several experiments. Your geographically distributed team needs a platform that delivers the most effective real-time collaboration and fast experimentation. You plan to add GPUs to accelerate the experimentation cycle and want to avoid manually provisioning infrastructure. You want to follow Google’s recommended approach. What should you do?

options.text: Configure a managed Dataproc cluster for large-scale data processing. Configure individual Jupyter notebooks on VMs that each team member uses for experimentation and model development.
Use Colab Enterprise with Cloud Storage for data management. Use a Git repository for version control.
Use Vertex AI Workbench and Cloud Storage for data management. Use a Git repository for version control.
Configure a distributed JupyterLab instance that each team member can access on a Compute Engine VM. Use a shared code repository for version control.

questions.explanation:
Colab Enterprise provides collaborative notebooks and managed compute: it provisions runtimes as needed, supports configurable accelerators including GPUs, and avoids the need to manage notebook infrastructure. Cloud Storage provides centralized data management, while a Git repository supports version control for the team’s work.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Colab Enterprise](https://docs.cloud.google.com/colab/docs/introduction) · [Runtimes and runtime templates](https://docs.cloud.google.com/colab/docs/runtimes)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to design a customized deep neural network in Keras to predict customer purchases from their purchase history. You want to explore model performance across multiple model architectures, store training data, and compare evaluation metrics in the same dashboard. What should you do?

options.text: Create multiple models using AutoML Tables.
Automate multiple training runs using Cloud Composer.
Run multiple training jobs on AI Platform with similar job names.
Create an experiment in Kubeflow Pipelines to organize multiple runs.

questions.explanation:
A Kubeflow Pipelines experiment groups related pipeline runs, allowing different model architectures to be executed and organized together. The Kubeflow Pipelines UI can compare the results of one or more runs within an experiment, while pipeline artifacts and metadata provide tracking for training data and evaluation outputs.

**Learn more:** [Kubeflow Pipelines: Experiment](https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/components/pipelines/concepts/experiment/) · [Kubeflow Pipelines: Interfaces](https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/components/pipelines/interfaces/)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You created a Python module using Keras to train a regression model. Within the same module, you developed two model architectures: linear regression and a deep neural network (DNN). You use the `training_method` argument to choose one of the two methods, and use the `learning_rate` and `num_hidden_layers` arguments in the DNN. You plan to use Vertex AI's hypertuning service with a budget of 100 trials. You want to determine the model architecture and hyperparameter values that minimize training loss and maximize model performance. What should you do?

options.text: Run one hypertuning job for 100 trials. Set num_hidden_layers as a conditional hyperparameter based on its parent hyperparameter training_method, and set learning_rate as a non-conditional hyperparameter.

Run two separate hypertuning jobs, a linear regression job for 50 trials, and a DNN job for 50 trials. Compare their final performance on a common validation set, and select the set of hyperparameters with the least training loss.

Run one hypertuning job with training_method as the hyperparameter for 50 trials. Select the architecture with the lowest training loss, and further hypertune it and its corresponding hyperparameters tor 50 trials.
Run one hypertuning job for 100 trials. Set num_hidden_layers and learning_rate as conditional hyperparameters based on their parent hyperparameter training_method.

questions.explanation:
Vertex AI conditional hyperparameters are added to a trial only when the specified parent hyperparameter has a matching value. Defining both `num_hidden_layers` and `learning_rate` as conditional on `training_method` lets one 100-trial job evaluate both architectures while tuning DNN-specific settings only for DNN trials and keeping learning-rate tuning independent for the two training methods.

**Learn more:** [Vertex AI: Overview of hyperparameter tuning](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/training/hyperparameter-tuning-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company operates an ecommerce website. You developed an ML model that recommends additional products to users in near real time based on the items currently in a user’s cart. The workflow will include these processes:  
  
1. The website will send a Pub/Sub message containing the relevant data, then receive a Pub/Sub message with the prediction.  
2. Predictions will be saved in BigQuery.  
3. The model will be kept in a Cloud Storage bucket and updated frequently.  
  
You want to minimize prediction latency and the effort needed to update the model. How should you reconfigure the architecture?

options.text: Write a Cloud Function that loads the model into memory for prediction. Configure the function to be triggered when messages are sent to Pub/Sub.
Create a pipeline in Vertex AI Pipelines that performs preprocessing, prediction, and postprocessing. Configure the pipeline to be triggered by a Cloud Function when messages are sent to Pub/Sub.
Expose the model as a Vertex AI endpoint. Write a custom DoFn in a Dataflow job that calls the endpoint for prediction.
Use the RunInference API with WatchFilePattern in a Dataflow job that wraps around the model and serves predictions.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Dataflow's RunInference transform performs model inference in the streaming pipeline, providing optimized local model memory management and avoiding the additional request path of a remote prediction endpoint. Its automatic model-refresh capability uses WatchFilePattern to detect the newest matching model file in Cloud Storage and update the model handler while the pipeline is running, without redeploying the pipeline. This supports low-latency Pub/Sub-driven predictions while accommodating frequent model updates.

**Learn more:** [Automatic model refresh | Cloud Dataflow](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/machine-learning/ml-model-refresh) · [RunInference transform best practices | Cloud Dataflow](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/machine-learning/runinference-best-practices)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a subscription-based company and have trained an ensemble of trees and neural networks to predict customer churn—the likelihood that customers will not renew their annual subscription.  
  
The average prediction is a 15% churn rate, but the model predicts that a particular customer is 70% likely to churn. This customer has a product-usage history of 30%, is located in New York City, and became a customer in 1997.  
  
You need to explain the difference between the actual 70% churn-rate prediction and the average prediction. You want to use Vertex Explainable AI. What should you do?

options.text: Train local surrogate models to explain individual predictions.
Configure sampled Shapley explanations on Vertex Explainable AI.
Configure integrated gradients explanations on Vertex Explainable AI.
Measure the effect of each feature as the weight of the feature multiplied by the feature value.

questions.explanation:
Sampled Shapley assigns feature attributions for an individual prediction relative to a baseline prediction and is recommended by Vertex Explainable AI for non-differentiable models, including ensembles of trees and neural networks.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Vertex Explainable AI](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/explainable-ai/overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to rapidly build and train a model that predicts the sentiment of customer reviews using custom categories, without writing code. You do not have sufficient data to train a model from scratch. The resulting model must have high predictive performance. Which service should you use?

options.text: AutoML Natural Language
Cloud Natural Language API
AI Hub pre-made Jupyter Notebooks
AI Platform Training built-in algorithms

questions.explanation:
AutoML Natural Language supports no-code training of high-quality custom text models, including custom sentiment analysis and content classification, using labeled training data and Google’s AutoML technology. The Cloud Natural Language API instead supplies pretrained language-analysis capabilities and does not train a custom model for user-defined categories.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Natural Language product overview](https://cloud.google.com/natural-language) · [Cloud Natural Language documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/natural-language/docs)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You developed a fraud-detection model for a large financial institution with Vertex AI. Although the model has high accuracy, stakeholders are worried about possible bias related to customer demographics. You have been asked to gain insight into the model's decision-making process and identify any fairness concerns. What should you do?

options.text: Create feature groups using Vertex AI Feature Store to segregate customer demographic features and non-demographic features. Retrain the model using only non-demographic features.
Use feature attribution in Vertex AI to analyze model predictions and the impact of each feature on the model's predictions.

Enable Vertex AI Model Monitoring to detect training-serving skew. Configure an alert to send an email when the skew or drift for a modes feature exceeds a predefined threshold. Re-train the model by appending new data to existing raining data.
Compile a dataset of unfair predictions. Use Vertex AI Vector Search to identify similar data points in the model's predictions. Report these data points to the stakeholders.

questions.explanation:
Vertex AI feature attribution shows how much each input feature contributes to a prediction. Reviewing attributions across predictions can reveal whether demographic attributes, or proxy attributes, disproportionately influence fraud decisions and provides an interpretable basis for investigating fairness concerns. Attribution should be supplemented with appropriate training-data and evaluation-metric analysis; it does not by itself establish that a model is fair or unbiased.

**Learn more:** [Vertex AI Explanation reference](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1beta1/Explanation) · [Vertex Explainable AI limitations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/explainable-ai/limitations)

questions.explanation:
Labels provide scalable, descriptive key-value metadata for categorizing AI Platform resources and filtering resource lists. AI Platform supports labels on jobs and models, and model versions also support labels, so consistently applying labels organizes shared resources without creating unnecessary project separation or access restrictions.

**Learn more:** [gcloud ai-platform jobs update](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/ai-platform/jobs/update) · [gcloud ai-platform models create](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/ai-platform/models/create)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team is developing an application for a global bank that millions of customers will use. You created a forecasting model that predicts customers’ account balances 3 days ahead. The team will use its results in a new feature that notifies users when their account balance is expected to fall below $25. How should you serve the predictions?

options.text: 1. Create a Pub/Sub topic for each user. 2. Deploy a Cloud Function that sends a notification when your model predicts that a user's account balance will drop below the $25 threshold.

1. Create a Pub/Sub topic for each user. 2. Deploy an application on the App Engine standard environment that sends a notification when your model predicts that a user's account balance will drop below the $25 threshold.

1. Build a notification system on Firebase. 2. Register each user with a user ID on the Firebase Cloud Messaging server, which sends a notification when the average of all account balance predictions drops below the $25 threshold.

1. Build a notification system on Firebase. 2. Register each user with a user ID on the Firebase Cloud Messaging server, which sends a notification when your model predicts that a user's account balance will drop below the $25 threshold.

questions.explanation:
A balance alert must be evaluated and delivered for each individual customer’s forecast. Firebase Cloud Messaging supports targeted notifications to registered client app instances, whereas calculating an average of all balance predictions would not identify a particular customer who is likely to fall below the threshold. Creating a separate Pub/Sub topic for every user is also an unsuitable per-user notification design at this scale.

**Learn more:** [Firebase Cloud Messaging overview](https://firebase.google.com/docs/cloud-messaging) · [Send a message using the FCM HTTP v1 API](https://firebase.google.com/docs/cloud-messaging/send/v1-api)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You recently built a wide-and-deep model in TensorFlow. You created training datasets using a SQL script that preprocesses raw data in BigQuery through instance-level data transformations. You need to build a training pipeline that retrains the model weekly. The trained model will generate daily recommendations. You want to minimize model-development and training time. How should you build the training pipeline?

options.text: Use the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK to implement the pipeline. Use the BigQueryJobOp component to run the preprocessing script and the CustomTrainingJobOp component to launch a Vertex AI training job.
Use the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK to implement the pipeline. Use the DataflowPythonJobOp component to preprocess the data and the CustomTrainingJobOp component to launch a Vertex AI training job.

Use the TensorFlow Extended SDK to implement the pipeline Use the ExampleGen component with the BigQuery executor to ingest the data the Transform component to preprocess the data, and the Trainer component to launch a Vertex AI training job.

Use the TensorFlow Extended SDK to implement the pipeline Implement the preprocessing steps as part of the input_fn of the model. Use the ExampleGen component with the BigQuery executor to ingest the data and the Trainer component to launch a Vertex AI training job.

questions.explanation:
Reusing the existing BigQuery SQL preprocessing preserves the established instance-level transformations and avoids rebuilding them in Dataflow or TFX. A Kubeflow Pipelines workflow can orchestrate the BigQuery preprocessing job and use `CustomTrainingJobOp` to run custom TensorFlow training in Vertex AI, providing the required weekly retraining flow with the least additional development.

**Learn more:** [Google Cloud Pipeline Components overview](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/pipelines/components-introduction) · [CustomJob components for Vertex AI Pipelines](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/pipelines/customjob-component)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You recently joined an enterprise-scale company with thousands of datasets. You know that each BigQuery table has an accurate description, and you need to locate the appropriate BigQuery table for a model you are building on AI Platform. How should you find the data you need?

options.text: Use Data Catalog to search the BigQuery datasets by using keywords in the table description.
Tag each of your model and version resources on AI Platform with the name of the BigQuery table that was used for training.
Maintain a lookup table in BigQuery that maps the table descriptions to the table ID. Query the lookup table to find the correct table ID for the data that you need.

Execute a query in BigQuery to retrieve all the existing table names in your project using the INFORMATION_SCHEMA metadata tables that are native to BigQuery. Use the result o find the table that you need.

questions.explanation:
Data Catalog automatically catalogs metadata for BigQuery resources, including tables, and supports searches using a `description:` query predicate. Searching table descriptions by keyword is therefore the appropriate catalog-wide method for discovering the needed BigQuery table.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a company that offers an anti-spam service that flags and hides spam posts on social-media platforms. The company currently uses a list of 200,000 keywords to identify suspected spam posts. When a post contains more than a few of these keywords, it is identified as spam. You want to begin using machine learning to flag spam posts for human review. What is the primary advantage of implementing machine learning for this business case?

options.text: Posts can be compared to the keyword list much more quickly.
New problematic phrases can be identified in spam posts.
A much longer keyword list can be used to flag spam posts.
Spam posts can be flagged using far fewer keywords.

questions.explanation:
Machine-learning spam classifiers learn patterns from examples of spam and legitimate content, rather than relying solely on a fixed keyword list. This enables the service to detect new problematic phrases and other variations that were not explicitly added as keywords.

**Learn more:** [What is Supervised Learning?](https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-supervised-learning) · [How spam detection taught us better tech support](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/how-spam-detection-taught-us-better-tech-support)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You recently trained an AutoML regression model with BigQuery ML. Alter the model by using BigQuery ML, and specify Vertex AI as the model registry. Deploy the model from Vertex AI Model Registry to a Vertex AI endpoint.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team is developing a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based architecture from scratch. questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company operates a video-sharing website where users can watch and upload videos. questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a training pipeline for a new XGBoost classification model using tabular data. The data resides in a BigQuery table. You must complete these steps:

You received a training-serving skew alert from a Vertex AI Model Monitoring job operating in production. You retrained the model using more recent training data and redeployed it to the Vertex AI endpoint, but you continue to receive the same alert. What should you do?

options.text: Update the model monitoring job to use a lower sampling rate.
Update the model monitoring job to use the more recent training data that was used to retrain the model.
Temporarily disable the alert. Enable the alert again after a sufficient amount of new production traffic has passed through the Vertex AI endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Vertex AI training-serving skew detection evaluates serving-feature distributions against the monitoring job’s configured training dataset baseline. Updating that baseline to the newer dataset used to retrain the deployed model aligns the comparison with the current model; changing sampling, disabling alerts, or retraining again does not update the baseline.

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for an online retailer. Use Vertex AI Forecast to build a NN-based model.
Use BigQuery ML to build a statistical ARIMA_PLUS model.
Use TensorFlow on Vertex AI Training to build a custom model.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery ML ARIMA_PLUS provides SQL-based time-series forecasting directly on data in BigQuery. A `TIME_SERIES_ID_COL` can identify each product, allowing many product sales series to be trained and forecast together; this is well suited to thousands of monthly product forecasts without the operational work of a custom Vertex AI training solution.

**Learn more:** [The CREATE MODEL statement for ARIMA_PLUS models](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-create-time-series)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a small company that has deployed an ML model with autoscaling on Vertex AI to serve online predictions in a production environment. The current model receives about 20 prediction requests per hour, with an average response time of one second.  
  
You retrained the same model on a new batch of data and are now canary testing it, directing ~10% of production traffic to the new model. During this canary test, prediction requests for the new model take between 30 and 180 seconds to complete. What should you do?

options.text: Submit a request to raise your project quota to ensure that multiple prediction services can run concurrently.
Turn off auto-scaling for the online prediction service of your new model. Use manual scaling with one node always available.
Remove your new model from the production environment. Compare the new model and existing model codes to identify the cause of the performance bottleneck.

Remove your new model from the production environment. For a short trial period, send all incoming prediction requests to BigQuery. Request batch predictions from your new model, and then use the Data Labeling Service to validate your model’s performance before promoting it to production.

questions.explanation:
At approximately two canary requests per hour, autoscaling can scale the new model down between requests, and a later request must wait for serving capacity to become available. Configuring manual scaling with one node continuously available keeps a replica warm and avoids scale-up latency. Vertex AI supports configuring a deployed model’s minimum replica count; scale-to-zero requires `min_replica_count=0` and requests arriving while scaled to zero must wait for scale-up.

**Learn more:** [Scale inference nodes using autoscaling](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/autoscaling)

options.text: Convert the speech to text and extract sentiments based on the sentences.
Convert the speech to text and build a model based on the words.
Extract sentiment directly from the voice recordings.
Convert the speech to text and extract sentiment using syntactical analysis.

questions.explanation:
Sentence-level sentiment analysis on speech-to-text transcripts uses the semantic content of what was said while avoiding direct use of acoustic voice features that can reveal or correlate with gender, age, accent, and cultural background. Sentence context is also necessary to interpret sentiment reliably; isolated words or syntax alone do not provide equivalent sentiment meaning. Amazon Comprehend sentiment analysis operates on text documents and returns positive, negative, neutral, or mixed sentiment.

**Learn more:** [Sentiment — Amazon Comprehend](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/how-sentiment.html) · [DetectSentiment — Amazon Comprehend API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/APIReference/API_DetectSentiment.html)

questions.explanation:
A dedicated service account limits the workload identity to the permissions explicitly granted to it, including the Vertex AI User role. Granting each intended team member Service Account User on that service account provides the required `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` capability for the instance, and granting Notebook Viewer restricts notebook visibility to those members. Google Cloud recommends using a custom service account rather than the default Compute Engine service account because the default account can have broad project permissions.

questions.explanation:
Vertex AI example-based explanations help investigate confident misclassifications by retrieving similar examples in the model’s latent representation, which can reveal mislabeled or confusing data. options.text: Use Vertex Al Pipelines to execute the experiments. Query the results stored in MetadataStore using the Vertex Al API.
Use Vertex Al Training to execute the experiments. Write the accuracy metrics to BigQuery, and query the results using the BigQuery API.
Use Vertex Al Training to execute the experiments. Write the accuracy metrics to Cloud Monitoring, and query the results using the Monitoring API.
Use Vertex Al Workbench user-managed notebooks to execute the experiments. Collect the results in a shared Google Sheets file, and query the results using the Google Sheets API.

questions.explanation:
Vertex AI Pipelines provides repeatable execution of ML workflows and captures pipeline-run parameters and metrics in Vertex ML Metadata. That metadata supports programmatic querying and comparison of experimental runs, avoiding the manual metric-export work required when using BigQuery, Cloud Monitoring, or a spreadsheet as the tracking system.

**Learn more:** [Introduction to Vertex ML Metadata](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/ml-metadata/introduction) · [Visualize and analyze pipeline results](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/pipelines/visualize-pipeline)

options.text: Configure the machines of the first two worker pools to have GPUs, and to use a container image where your training code runs. Configure the third worker pool to have GPUs, and use the reductionserver container image.

Configure the machines of the first two worker pools to have GPUs and to use a container image where your training code runs. Configure the third worker pool to use the reductionserver container image without accelerators, and choose a machine type that prioritizes bandwidth.

Configure the machines of the first two worker pools to have TPUs and to use a container image where your training code runs. Configure the third worker pool without accelerators, and use the reductionserver container image without accelerators, and choose a machine type that prioritizes bandwidth.

Configure the machines of the first two pools to have TPUs, and to use a container image where your training code runs. Configure the third pool to have TPUs, and use the reductionserver container image.

questions.explanation:
Vertex AI Reduction Server uses GPU-based primary and worker pools to run the training workload. The third worker pool runs dedicated reducer nodes using the Reduction Server container image; reducers do not use GPUs, and their aggregate network bandwidth must match or exceed that of the first two worker pools. A bandwidth-prioritized CPU machine type is therefore appropriate for the third pool.

**Learn more:** [Distributed training — Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/training/distributed-training)

",["$","$L57",null,{"choices":{"A":"Convert the speech to text and extract sentiments based on the sentences.","B":"Convert the speech to text and build a model based on the words.","C":"Extract sentiment directly from the voice recordings.","D":"Convert the speech to text and extract sentiment using syntactical analysis."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"Sentence-level sentiment analysis on speech-to-text transcripts uses the semantic content of what was said while avoiding direct use of acoustic voice features that can reveal or correlate with gender, age, accent, and cultural background. You are an analyst at a large banking firm. You are developing a robust, scalable ML pipeline to train several regression and classification models. Your primary pipeline focus is model interpretability. You want to productionize the pipeline as quickly as possible. What should you do?

options.text: Use Tabular Workflow for Wide & Deep through Vertex AI Pipelines to jointly train wide linear models and deep neural networks
Use Google Kubernetes Engine to build a custom training pipeline for XGBoost-based models
Use Tabular Workflow for TabNet through Vertex AI Pipelines to train attention-based models
Use Cloud Composer to build the training pipelines for custom deep learning-based models

questions.explanation:
Tabular Workflow for TabNet is a fully managed Vertex AI Pipelines workflow for classification and regression. Its sequential-attention architecture identifies the features used in decisions, providing inherent model interpretability, while Vertex AI integration enables rapid production deployment without building and operating a custom training platform.

**Learn more:** [Tabular Workflows on Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/tabular-data/tabular-workflows/overview)

You are an ML engineer at a social-media company developing a visual filter for users’ profile photos. This requires training an ML model that detects bounding boxes around human faces. You want to use the filter in your company’s iOS-based mobile-phone application, while minimizing code development and ensuring the model is optimized for inference on mobile phones. What should you do?

options.text: Train a model using AutoML Vision and use the “export for Core ML” option.
Train a model using AutoML Vision and use the “export for Coral” option.
Train a model using AutoML Vision and use the “export for TensorFlow.js” option.
Train a custom TensorFlow model and convert it to TensorFlow Lite (TFLite).

questions.explanation:
Using AutoML Vision object detection minimizes code development because you train without writing custom model code, and the requirement is an iOS app, so exporting for Core ML (A) yields a model in Apple's native on-device inference format that is optimized for iPhone hardware. Core ML is exactly the runtime iOS uses for efficient mobile inference. The Coral export (B) targets Edge TPU hardware, not iOS phones, and TensorFlow.js (C) targets web/JavaScript environments, so neither fits an iOS mobile app. Training a custom TensorFlow model and converting to TFLite (D) does produce a mobile model but requires substantially more model development, violating the minimize-code requirement, and TFLite is not the native iOS format.

**Learn more:** [AutoML models on Apple platforms](https://firebase.google.com/docs/ml/ios/detect-objects-with-automl) · [AutoML Vision Edge export formats](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/announcing-updates-to-automl-vision-edge-automl-video-and-video-intelligence-api)

questions.explanation:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is effective for grounding a model in factual or reference knowledge so it can answer questions accurately, but it does not retrain or adapt the model's underlying generative behavior. Since the model keeps defaulting to Python-like syntax, it needs to learn the actual generative patterns and structure of MechScript, which is a skill-acquisition problem, not a knowledge-retrieval problem. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on a curated dataset of valid MechScript code examples directly updates the model's weights so it learns the correct syntax, structure, and idioms of the proprietary language, resolving the hallucination of incorrect syntax in a way that simply retrieving more reference chunks or stuffing the manual into the prompt cannot achieve.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a financial company that has a large custom dataset containing one trillion tokens. You are building a chatbot powered by Gemini to answer onboarding questions using five PDF onboarding documents stored in Cloud Storage. These documents get updated on an as-needed basis, either weekly or monthly. You anticipate that the application will handle a high volume of repeated user queries against this same documentation context.  
  
You want to choose the most appropriate and cost-effective approach for managing this context so that the chatbot always has current information. What should you do?

options.text: Fine-tune a Gemini model using the text from the five PDF files as a training dataset.
Send requests with the five PDF files as content pointing to the URI file. Use implicit context caching.
Create an explicit context cache using the five PDF files, and regenerate the cache when the source files change.
Create an explicit context cache using the five PDF files. Set a time-to-live (TTL) of seven days, and regenerate the cache every seven days.

questions.explanation:
Explicit context caching lets you store the tokenized representation of the five PDF files once and reuse it across many repeated requests, substantially lowering cost and latency for high-volume queries that reference the same context. Because the source documents change irregularly (weekly or monthly, as needed) rather than on a fixed schedule, the cache should be explicitly invalidated and rebuilt only when the underlying PDFs actually change — this guarantees the chatbot never serves stale answers while avoiding unnecessary cache regeneration overhead when the documents haven't changed. A fixed weekly TTL either risks serving outdated content between refresh cycles or triggers needless regeneration when updates occur less frequently than weekly. Fine-tuning is not designed for frequently changing reference documents and would require costly retraining after every update. Implicit caching lacks guaranteed cache hits and explicit control over cache freshness, making it unsuitable when up-to-date, cost-predictable performance is required.

**Learn more:** [Context caching | Gemini API](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/caching)

You want this transition to be transparent and require no modifications to the client application that calls the endpoint.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Deploy the new model to a serverless Cloud Run service. Implement logic in the client application that routes 10% of user requests to the Cloud Run service and the rest to the original endpoint.
Deploy the new model to the Agent Platform endpoint where the current model is deployed. Configure the endpoint’s traffic split to allocate 10% of user requests to the new model.

Create two separate Agent Platform Pipelines, one for each model version. Use Agent Platform Experiments to run both pipelines simultaneously. Configure the experiment to send 10% of user requests to the new model’s pipeline and the rest to the production model’s pipeline.
Deploy the new model to a new Agent Platform endpoint. Configure Cloud Load Balancing to send 10% of user requests to the new endpoint and the rest to the original endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Vertex AI (Agent Platform) endpoints allow multiple model versions to be deployed simultaneously to a single endpoint, each with an assigned traffic percentage. By deploying the new model to the same endpoint already serving the current model and setting the traffic split to send 10% of requests to the new model and 90% to the existing one, the platform handles routing internally. The client application continues to call the same endpoint URL/DNS name, so no changes to the client are needed, and the split can be adjusted or rolled back at any time without redeploying infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Split traffic between models on an endpoint](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/deploy-model-console#update_traffic_split) · [Deploy a model to an endpoint](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/deploy-model-api)

options.text: Fine-tune the latest Llama model from Model Garden on Agent Platform Serverless Training.
Use the latest Gemini Flash foundational model.
Deploy the latest Llama model from Model Garden, and use prompt engineering.
Fine-tune a BERT-based model from Hugging Face.

questions.explanation:
Fine-tuning is the appropriate technique when you have a large labeled dataset and need the model to deeply internalize specific stylistic patterns (such as mimicking particular authors) rather than relying on surface-level prompting. Vertex AI Model Garden provides open models like Llama that can be fine-tuned using custom training jobs (e.g., via parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods such as LoRA) on your own dataset, and the resulting fine-tuned model can then be deployed to a custom VM, satisfying the hosting requirement. Encoder-only models like BERT are not designed for open-ended text generation, Gemini Flash cannot be deployed on a custom VM since it is only available as a managed API, and prompt engineering alone without fine-tuning would not fully exploit the large author-specific dataset to achieve deep stylistic mimicry.

**Learn more:** [Vertex AI Model Garden - Llama 3.1 Finetuning notebook](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/vertex-ai-samples/blob/main/notebooks/community/model_garden/model_garden_pytorch_llama3_1_finetuning.ipynb) · [Fine-Tuning Large Language Models: How Vertex AI Takes LLMs to the Next Level](https://codelabs.developers.google.com/llm-finetuning-supervised)

You are the lead ML engineer for a large ecommerce company. The Data Analytics team has prepared a dataset of 50 million transaction rows, stored in a partitioned BigQuery table. The team is made up primarily of SQL experts who have limited experience with Python or TensorFlow.  
  
You need to build a binary classification model that predicts the likelihood of a customer making a purchase within the next seven days. Predictions must be provided as a daily batch job.  
  
Your solution should minimize:  
  
- Development effort  
- Data movement  
- Overall solution complexity  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a model with BigQuery ML that includes the MODEL_TYPE=AUTOML_CLASSIFIER settings. Use the ML.PREDICT function to generate predictions as part of your nightly data warehouse jobs.

Use the BigQuery ML TRANSFORM function to normalize and scale numerical features, one-hot encode categorical features, and train a MODEL_TYPE=LOGISTIC_REG mode. Use the ML.PREDICT function to generate predictions as part of your nightly data warehouse jobs.
Train a classification model with Agent Platform AutoML Tabular Workflows, deploy the trained model to an Agent Platform endpoint, and add a nightly Cloud Run job to trigger batch predictions.

Develop an XGBoost model on an Agent Platform Workbench notebook. Load the data into a pandas DataFrame, and pickle it to a Cloud Storage bucket. Create another notebook that loads the pickled model from Cloud Storage and saves predictions back to Cloud Storage. Schedule this notebook for nightly execution.

questions.explanation:
Because the data already lives in BigQuery and the team is SQL-proficient, BigQuery ML is the right platform, keeping training and inference in place with no data export. Using MODEL_TYPE=AUTOML_CLASSIFIER in the CREATE MODEL statement lets BigQuery ML automatically handle feature engineering, normalization, encoding, and model/architecture selection, so no manual TRANSFORM logic, Python code, or separate ML infrastructure is required. Running ML.PREDICT against the table as part of the nightly warehouse jobs produces the required daily batch predictions with minimal added complexity. In contrast, manually building a TRANSFORM clause for LOGISTIC_REG adds unnecessary development effort, and exporting data to Vertex AI Workbench/pandas or deploying an AutoML Tabular Workflow endpoint with Cloud Run orchestration introduces unnecessary data movement and infrastructure complexity that the SQL-focused team is not equipped to manage.

**Learn more:** [The CREATE MODEL statement for AutoML models | BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-create-automl) · [Introduction to ML in BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/bqml-introduction)
